reviews.review: Great show by a group called the Biggish Band, they rocked the house last night. I will definitely be returning for a show.

Wouldn't risk going here!! I booked a table for 2 for my boyfriend's birthday last Thursday. It was a VERY special occasion. I'd spent hours selecting the exact right jazz dinner venue, which I had determined was Minton's.  I bought tickets through Eventbrite for the Alan Bartus Trio. Researched them too and they looked awesome. I called the manager of Minton's beforehand to find out if it would be appropriate to talk during the show. He was very pleasant, said yes, and also encouraged me to come as early as 7:00 for the 8:00 show so that we would be able to chat before the music started. When we arrived at Minton's we were both as excited as can be. But the lights were off and the door was locked shut. It was as dark as a haunted house. There was a white piece of paper taped on the door saying "CLOSED".  We were in disbelief. There were also 4 women vacationing from North Carolina there to celebrate one of their birthdays as well.  They were also completely shocked and disheartened. It was their first day of vacation in New York City and this is how they're greeted. We had all excitedly come all the way up to Harlem for this special evening and Minton's GHOSTS us. I still don't have my $48 dollars back that I paid for the jazz tickets. Minton's still hasn't answered my calls. That evening, the manager of the building next door called Minton's ownership, and they simply said, "We will not be opening this evening." Who does this? Never in my life has such a randomly strange thing happened to me in my dining out experiences.  I feel badly for myself and my guest of course - but even more sad and embarrassed for the lovely ladies from North Carolina who had come to NYC to celebrate a birthday with an evening of great food and jazz.  I don't know what's going on with Minton's and I would obviously never risk making reservations there ever again.

I came here with a group of friends for a birthday dinner. It's a pretty laid-back spot with great service and live entertainment. They have different bands daily so you can actually check online to see who's playing. The real winner of the night for me, was the ribeye steak. It was super juicy, flavored with rosemary and garlic, and had nice marbling. Overall the place was very nice. I'll be back again just for that steak!

So my first night in the city started out at Minton's Playhouse which is black owned and a legendary spot for amazing live jazz music. My media mentors booked a table here which was in the front by the stage which was great because it was not too loud where we were shouting at each other. 

We started out with a toast and cheers to the weekend, I ordered the sweet notes which is a tequila and strawberry based cocktail. Whew, this drink was strong! I'm not complaining but be mindful if you decided to sip on a few of these like most of us did. The sounds of the live music added to the amazing ambience and scenery of Minton's. It's definitely a grown and sexy vibe, which I loved! When mingling with some of the locals, I was informed that it was Harlem Music/Jazz Week, so it was packed to the brim inside. 

The downside is it took quite a bit of time for the food to come out. We had about 2 - 3 drinks prior to the food coming out, so some of us were definitely ready to dive into some food. 

The truffle fries were crispy and good, nothing too life changing. However, that grilled snapper though! I was expecting it to be the whole fish - with the head and tail but it was I didn't read it closely to see that it was a filet. It was well seasoned, I want to say it was jerk marinade and seasoning. It was very moist and so yummy. It came with a butter sauce, jasmine rice, and asparagus. The food was very good but it just took a while to come out. Overall, a great experience and I would definitely return for a cocktail and the vibes of the live jazz band.

$25 cover (unsure if this price changes per booking) for Amazing Band (sound needs a bit of work) but a great band knows how to work with what they got and bring the house down. I wish the tables faced the stage because how it is is killing my neck.

Although drinks are on the sweeter side with a bit of food it helps to alter the taste buds (or wait for the ice to melt a bit. It always helps.) The small bites leave a bit to be desired but they do the trick if you've eaten a meal elsewhere and are just hankering for a small bite.

Overall a great spot for an intimate or party night out (depends on the band really). Spots 100% worth a trek from all the way yonder.

Had an absolute blast here on a Friday Night after Dinner. Ambiance is cozy and romantic. The staff was very efficient and attentive. We're from Houston so I loved the multicultural atmosphere. The Band was amazing and you could tell they love what they do. I would absolutely recommend this spot for any music lovers...it gets packed after 11, so get there early if you want a good seat.

The way this place is run is terrible. Shameful that the Management is so bad for a historic place.

We went for a dinner time performance and there was a loud obnoxious table being so loud that it was distracting even to the performers on stage. We asked the staff/server if there was anything they could do since it was very disruptive and they said "no because that is the owner" which completely blew my mind at that level of unprofessionalism and basic decency especially from Management. On top of the extremely slow service and mediocre food we decided to just leave. Not supporting this establishment again. There are better Jazz lounges in Harlem and NYC.

Came here for my friend's grandmother's memorial service and it was really nice. The staff was attentive and really accommodating. We had the place all to ourselves with the chairs set up in a circle. Due the the size, it felt very intimate. The food was very tasty (although I would have preferred it a bit hotter). 

I've also come here for jazz on a Saturday night, when the tables and chairs were set up normally, and it was very memorable as well. Great venue with great food!

I went there this past Saturday for my b day weekend. Was very excited however we ordered coffee, empanadas and drinks. The coffee was cold when they brought it. I asked them to heat up and they heated so much I couldn't drink it. The empanadas was terrible and it smelled bad. I thought the food was going to be great but it was terrible. I did enjoy the music however I wanted the entire experience to be great.

I came to Minton's last night. From the beginning, I was greeted and seated. The host lowered the AC because it was a bit chilly. My guest and I got the 32oz option drink. Their drinks are strong and pack a nice punch. Before each set, they give you an overview of Minton's history and performers. The food is delicious! I ordered the veggie empanadas and they were so tasty! The performer Denise King was incredible!! I highly recommend this place if you are looking for a date night, solo night out or just to listen to some good live music!

Minton's is a historic Harlem jazz venue and supper club, and they continue to bring in great bands. Drinks and food are decent - but expect to pay higher price points here. I like to remind myself that I am supporting the artists and a storied live music venue. 

Tonight they added a 20% gratuity to my bill (for a table for 1) to "simplify my experience." I wouldn't be so upset by that, except that I barely saw my server during the second set. Could have at least used one refill on my water, if not another drink.

I went there for my favorite band The food and drinks are okay, but the side vegetables were horrible, didn't taste anything at all. 
Mist stuff are fine but this woman, I think she is a manager or something. She just look very rude, had attitude. May be she has some business skills that we can't tell, but I wouldn't hire anyone act like that front of the customers

Great food and loved Ted Nash 
will definitely atten again if they have good jazz performance

Last night was my first time at Minton's Playhouse. My experience there was great. Aaron Goldberg was performing, him and the band was were amazing. I got the chance to meet Aaron, he was so friendly and was kind enough to take a pic with me. 
For food I ordered lamb chops which came with a mango sauce, mashed potatoes and spinach which was really good. Along with a strong Margarita
Definitely grown and sexy vibes

We came to mintons to celebrate my mother's 65th birthday and it happened to be during restaurant week. They have this amazing deal that includes a $60 6 course tasting menu and each dish is paired with a wine. While you are eating you are able to watch a jazz performance as well. From the start the staff and manager Mark were super helpful with my questions to help plan the perfect night. The music sets were at 7 and 9 but he recommended us to come at 6 to make sure we had to get through all of the courses. He also told the performer ,who was amazing, that it was my mother's birthday so he was able to shout her out. 
The decor is super cute and I would definitely recommend for a date night. The crowd was mixed with younger and older folks of all different nationalities. The food was delicious. Everything that we had was flavorful. Being that it was the tasting menu it was smaller portions but at the end of the 6 courses I was full. There was even someone in my party that had a food allergy and they were willing to accommodate that and change out some of the items in the tasting menu for them. 
Would definitely recommend and will be coming back!
What an iconic place. The live music was beautiful, and it was fun hanging out in an elegant space.

AVOID at all costs! Touristy, mediocre food, OK drinks, 3rd class musicians. There are more interesting & worthy Jazz venues in NYC. This place lacks professionalism and quality of musicians. More like a local pub with unpleasant odor, mediocre shows featuring average commercial grade musicians. Don't waste your time & $$$. Go to more reputable Jazz venues with consistent history.

What a wonderful place. Glad I found this club located in Harlem inside the historic Cecil Hotel. 
Willie Alexander and Mo-Mo jammed!!! Great dinner club!! Shout out to Rafael too. Thank You for being apart of my birthday NYC experience!!!

Great music with a grown and sexy vibe. I had such a great time listening to the artists.some of them have performed at Mintons for years and even with some of the Jazz greats! The did a rendition of the Sanford and Son theme song that was amazing! The good was sooo good and and the portions were huge! I cannot wait to go back and support this amazing historical gem.

One of the most moving experiences  Dinner, drinks, amazing musicians, warm and comfy, part of Harlem Renaissance history. Amazing end to our Soul of Harlem walking tour (with Lawrence Henderson through Airbnb experiences https://abnb.me/kcamkXHbclb).
Such a fun vibe! Great service and food! And the music is just amazing! Will definitely visit again!
Love this place! The ambiance is absolutely a VIBE! Food was pretty good. Great music as well!

The staff and the way this place is run is horrible. Understaffed at the bar and kitchen, rude host, unattentive wait staff and just slow slow sloowww service. Such a shame for such a historic place. Food is mediocre. They also have the audacity to include a 20% tip for such crap service. 
Advice: grab a drink at the bar and enjoy the music, that's all!

The service, food, and drinks were all very poor. The server couldn't take our orders or be bothered to get them accurately, it took a literal hour for my drink to arrive, my Caesar salad was both over dressed and had sat on the line and came out fully soggy with zero crunch to it. The worst part was nobody seemed to have any sort of standard - it felt like a free for all including the manager. The only saving grace here and reason to visit is the incredible music. Eat and pre party before you arrive.

This place was really nice. I enjoyed the food & music but the vibe was the best. It's nice being able to go to places in Harlem instead of having to go all the way into the city. There's a cover charge and menu minimum which I believe changes upon the day but that's expected with any place that has live music or entertainment.

Went for the Saturday night Grupo Jazzón: "Summer Dream Team Dance Party!" Was simply amazing and the artist's mesmerized us with their musical skills. The drinks were delicious and place was top notch. I only wish they had played for  little longer. Show lasted exactly 60 minutes. Will definitely be going back again several times.

It's so sad what's happened to this place. The food is edible, but it's not very good. They need to get a REAL chef, like when they had JJ. The music is still great. Let's return this place to the glory it used to have and let's not lose another Harlem institution to cheap food that relies only on tourists.
Excellent atmosphere and music, great old fashioned from the bar and really liked the Lamb Burger! The ordering process after the show starts is a little confusing, but all in all a great time!

Wow this place exceeded expectations! Spent my last night in NYC here and it was well worth it. Food was honestly decadent, Mac and cheese was 10/10, would recommend with shrimp. Lobster ravioli was booomb, with shrimp it was it a 11/10. Live Performance was spectacular and will forever be in my most cherished memories. It is a must visit spot with a unique history as it is the birthplace of bepop jazz. Henny coladas were refreshing. Heads up: there is a $40 minimum per person and $20 donation to performance per person but well worth it and dinner + drink easily adds up to $40.

Man, it's good to have these guys back- and better than ever
More casual, broader menu - the sengalese   lamb dibib (?) - a knockout and so were the pork chops 
crazy generous cocktails (but order your own favorite off the menu) and the music, especially the Thursday night jam sessions with over the top  JJ and Benny.
Get acquainted before the big guys (blue note, Birdland, Dizzys and VV reopen)
You won't be sorry

Music was great- the front of the house tried to appease, but I have never had such a fatty rib-eye steak in my life!!! Just nasty! Without providing too much detail, I will highly recommend you EAT somewhere else and have drinks ONLY at mintons.. it was crap- check was enhanced by about 47. 00 for tip on a party of two - on top of musicians fee of 20 bucks each. I don't want anything made up to me- just a yucky birthday feeling! Don't GO!!!

The music is absolutely amazing. However, seems a little fishy that there's no cover charge and once you sit at a table there's a sign saying  $40. minimum per person. Why not tell people up front??? Also the food and drinks were not good. I will only tolerate the club in order to see a show.

I made a reservation at Minton's on Sunday evening in hopes of enjoying drinks and the live music while supporting local businesses during the pandemic which I do safely every weekend.

I double checked the website when making my reservation as I didn't see any indication showing where customers could contribute/tip the musicians- I assumed we'd have the option to do so at the restaurant. We ordered wine and snacks enjoying the set only to see an additional $40 "donation" charge.

I was more than willing to pay it but wanted to understand why it wasn't clearly stated on their website where they asked for card information to make a reservation, and said more than once there was no need for escalation- I simply wanted to understand the policy for future reference As I had cash more than the asked donation.

The server insisted on saying the owner would come talk to me which wasn't asked for or necessary. 

The owner who I will be specific and say is an old white male- came to our table and went on to accuse me of not being able to afford the charge, and further insult me and my guest who happen to be 2 black females who are formerly of the industry and support many local Harlem businesses and initiatives. 

In the current social and political climate, you'd hope that a non-POC male owner of an establishment in Harlem would have more business sense at a bare minimum. 

Horribly disappointed and disgusted, and the piece de resistance of insults was our server trying to offer me a $20 bill multiple times when trying to exit.

If I could give a zero I would. Never again and will tell anyone who asks to not step foot there.

Came here a while back for a SoFi Member Experience event.  It's in my neighborhood and I hadn't been so I felt an obligation to go.  This venue is world renounced and a part of Harlem's history so it's definitely a must see.  We had a special menu and the food was delicious as well as filling.  The band who performed for our event was top notch and you even had some means to talk to people in a less threatening or overwhelming setting.  I learned about another SoFi product I later used because of talking to a fellow member who was using it.  I don't know how this venue is when you're not going to a private event or on a normal night with normal hours but I had fun at the event I went to and would encourage anybody who considers themselves a jazz aficionado or well rounded on Harlem matters to stop by once they reopen.

Went here for my father's birthday back at the end of November 2019 and we had an excellent time. Our waitress was great and took care of us. The food came out a little slow but once it got here, it was good. My father had the vegetarian lasagna and said it was the best he's ever had which was a huge relief because I chose Minton's because he loves jazz music and more importantly he's a picky vegetarian. I had the chicken empanadas which was good (second best I've ever had) and I had Laura's chicken which was good but didn't blow me away. We then shared the cornbread which was good but not better than Red Rooster's (my father's favorite). 

The main problem I had was the close seating arrangements. I was practically sitting in someone's lap and could see everything they ordered and ate. Also be prepared to spend money. It's about $25 per person at door and you have to spend a certain amount when ordering food. Also if you make reservations on OpenTable and you need to cancel, they will charge you so be careful. From what I've gathered this place is a "hit" or "miss" and I'm glad it was a "hit" when I went.

First off, they had only two waiters on Valentines and they were fantastic. Management here is the problem. 

9:30 dinner res
10pm ordered dinner
11:30pm our dinner was sent to the wrong table
midnight, asked WTF is our dinner
10 minutes later they came out with our food. 

Why in THE F would you only have 2 waiters working on Valentines eve, when you clearly have a booking system telling you that you're oversubscribed and had to turn people away. Management should really be fired here. Morons.

Wow.  Where do I start... Firstly, if you are going to Miltons to have a drink, I'm sure its fine.  I, however, decided to throw my birthday brunch there and it was A SHIT SHOW!!  These people are so disorganized... its unbelievable.  From 4 weeks before the party to the night before, they just couldn't get it together. Their "events planner", Zamira is useless... nice person? Yes.  Able to help execute, or the type of person to remember details - NO!  My family explained that the waiter, Walter, was rude and tried to overcharge them. Not only that but the owner, Raphael is a bully!  I mean arguing with me by text at 1:30 am the night before the event??  Quoting me prices then raising them $200 increments the night before the event! This is experience was THE WORST!!! RUN DONT WALK the other direction.  I came here because my company had rented the room twice before.  That will no longer happen.  The saving grace was the housekeeper and coat check girl that helped me decorate the party as the owner sat there on his phone.  I wholeheartedly do not recommend this place.  
Horrible service
Incompetent
Terrible food.
Good rum punch - although this does not a business make.
Ugh - I'm so glad its over but feel a responsibility to warn the next person.

I have never left a Yelp review before but I feel the urge to especially how we've been treated. My husband and I came to Minton's for a great evening. We are still sitting here 2 hours  later after the first set is finished still waiting for our food. The two tables next to us who ordered after us received food before us and have finished their meal..... where is the organization to this? Never again. You've been warned.

Rough Night. We have been here many times to a seamless experience and a great set of music, even on a Valentines Day. Tonight, Valentines Day 2020, was a complete shit show. Apparently they sold tickets via eventbrite and also booked via open table. Everyone who showed up for the 930a set was waiting in the frigid cold while they determined who paid via Eventbrite and who just made reservations. Once seated 45 min later, we waited for menus since all of them had been doled out to the newly seated pat for it. The short-ish story is we were there from 9 - 12am and NEVER GOT OUR ENTREES. Couples next to us got their food, (whole steaks), one woman next to me ordered the same as me from the prix fix and received her food and polished it off. The band came and went, then we got an appetizer.... towards 11am we started to complain about the entrees and were told they were checking on it. I asked that the dessert be boxed up and we get the check when the entree came out. Still nothing. We were offered a discount of 20%, then 30% which we would have accepted had we actually gotten the food. We kept being told it was being boxed up to go and would come out, never did. We eventually got up and left, bc WTF? So disappointed in what used to be a consistently elegant establishment and experience!!

It's unfortunate that the person who was so anxious to insure that we took care of our cover charge does not have the same attention to detail when it comes to his own voice volume during the performance. He shows a disrespect for the beauty of Mr. Bey's voice as well as his own role as a person who should be setting an example for others to follow.

Thank you Zamira (fabulous events coordinator), staff and Minton's for making my Birthday spectacular!!!!!  They went above and beyond my expectations in ensuring that all of my guests were well attended to and comfortable.  The food was superb, music was outstanding, and the staff was great!!!!

Zamira was fantastic to work with and so, so, so accommodating.  She made feel like an absolute Queen on my special day- thank you!!!!!

reviews.review:
I have been a few times.  Each time the same..  Very unorganized, chaotic management.  Nice wait staff. Average food.  Music great. You really have to "want to" be here.  
This time worse. We were there tonight on time and they said the last show had not finished so they sent us away for 30 minutes.  We returned in 30 min. Only to stand in line  - outside in the rain- for another 30 min.  Then because "their computers were no working" we had to pay cash for the cover - (but dinner was later charged to a creDit card.).  And they demanded that we check our coats  - even tho we were shivering!!!   Absolutely ridiculous.  Will have to wait for enough time to pass to forget how annoying this was , to return.

This place is a Must visit.  We went to the Glow Brunch event.  Got the unlimited mimosa, eggs Benedict with filet mignon. Excellent!!. We had so much fun. The service and vibe was great and energetic.  We went to the 12pm brunch. The DJ played some great classics, and the live jazz band came afterwards. I will be coming back here.

We went to see King Solomon Hicks last night at Minton's. He is an exceptional talent. As a venue Minton's is terrific. We were warmly greeted at the door. The food is excellent. They are connected to Cicil's restaurant next door which must be equally great for food. The service was good, the feel of the place was very cozy, relaxing and welcoming. It was also nice that someone there, the management or the musicians, had figured out just the right volume on the guitar speakers. Not overly loud to ruin the experience. Overall a great night at a great place!

Jazz brunch in Harlem!

Great music, great food, fair prices. Minton's rocks. (It's actually Jazz, not Rock, but "Jazzes" wouldn't convey the same excitement. It would be confusing. So we'll go with "Minton's rocks").

Sunday brunch: you have to give your card to reserve the seats, but you Don't pay to get in (they'll bang you $75 bucks if you don't show, though). VERY reasonable prices, I got steak and eggs for $26 bucks. And it was no small steak, it was a good 12 oz. Cooked just right, tender and juicy. The vegetable empanadas were a real treat (make sure to ask for the cilantro/green tomato sauce), and the veggie burger is reportedly excellent.  The prix fixe menu looked equally enjoyable and affordable. 

My only criticism: Dear Management, what's with the coffee? This is New York City, we take our coffee seriously around here. It's brunch, get the coffee in front of me fast and bring the pot around frequent. The coffee was good and strong, but I was seated 20 minutes before the first cup showed up. Tip #2, when you bring the coffee and the sugar, bring the milk too. It was missing from every coffee service I saw. #3, when somebody asks for milk, bring it. I didn't get any until the 3rd cup. The servers are all nice as pie but I didn't see a lot of hustle. 

Ok, enough about that. I loved everything on the plate and I didn't have to eat again for a long time. 

The music! The Dennis Hernandez Trio played fun, exciting, brilliant Cuban jazz. They definitely met the calibre of performance you expect at Minton's. (Fun fact, Minton's was founded in 1938 and played a pivotal role in the development of bebop.) Everybody who's anybody has played there. Here's their Wikipedia page:  https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minton%27s_Playhouse

And what a beautiful place. Comfortable seating, very elegant, fun art on the wall behind the stage (see the pictures). 

You CAN NOT beat the value and the experience at Minton's. Bring your friends, they will hail you as a cool in-the-know New Yorker. DON'T bring a first date: you'll have nowhere to go but down after that. 

Five out of five stars! I will be back.
Cannot say enough about this place...food, delicious... atmosphere, quaint and intimate.  The music, fantastic!! Great experience...you will not be disappointed.

Great for brunch. The live music was a plus. We went to brunch for my Grandma mother's 90th birthday. Prix fix meals are a good option but your better off just ordering al la cart. Wait service was a bit slow. I would go again just for the live music.

I was so excited to go to Minton's as I'd heard a lot about this legendary  club.  As I walk into  the room the first thing  that catches my ear is that the piano is so out of tune aargh!   I look around to see where the sound engineer is and he was nowhere to be found as there were some balance issues with the music. 

This is a plea to the management!!!  
Please maintain your piano and have it tuned at least once a week and make sure that your engineer is by the board at all times during the show to make subtle adjustments. 

The room is beautiful and the staff was very friendly but fix the most important reason that you have a clientele and that is the entertainment. 

Thank you

I had a lovely experience going here. Every time I visit Cecil or Minton's I have a great experience. The decor walking into this place was to die for. The lovely jazz pictures, and the live band just made you get the OVERALL JAZZ experience. I went on a Sunday where the brunch menu is $55 it comes with a meal and unlimited mimosas. I decided to just eat brunch without the mimosas.  I decided to get the chicken and waffles which was $19. It came with about four pieces of chicken and a side of cream spinach, with mixed berries. The chicken was seasoned perfectly... 
My boyfriend got the Minton Pangacious which came with a filet of fish, shrimp and quinoa. .. he also ordered a side of Mac and cheese. The food was so good. 
I have to shout out LATEEF. Every time I enter the two restaurants he is so up to par. He has a well clean outfit on and is very attentive. He makes sure he waits with a smile. His suspenders are also a plus.... LATEEF is a great assets to this company. 
They also have a booklet of Minton's artwork which is a plus. 
The live band also made my food feel better..

Went to Minton's for the first time a couple weeks ago and had a great experience. My friend was friends with folks in the band so we probably received special treatment as a result. The food was wonderful and I really enjoyed the intimacy of the place. Seems important to get there early otherwise you're near the bar where you're not getting as much of a great experience with the jazz band. Mature crowd and fancy date night. I definitely recommend trying it once.
Buyers be warned... they overbook, so even if you purchase tickets in advance seating is not guaranteed. Very disappointing experience. Would not recommend.

Incredible music and food. This local jazz joint never disappoints! I've been here several times and it always amazes me. 10/10 would recommend Laura's Chicken for dinner with a nice bottle of wine. I WILL BE BACK!

Didnt like it at all. Their quite policy made us feel so uncomfortable. They didn't tell us from the beginning or when we made the reservation that there is a 25 dollars admission fee per person and another 30 dollars minimum consumption. I have been in very good restaurants and jazz bar around the world and I never heard about these polices, especially for the minimum consumption. Minton it s definitely not "the place" where you would be keen to go on a Saturday night. I wanted to hear some good music not to stay quite like attending a musical. 3 employees came and told me please don't laugh please, you speak too loud (and I wasn't). Rude, unprofessional. I won't recommend it

Such a great experience to be apart of history and know that the ambiance is still there....I was really excited to know that it is also added into the African American Black History Museum in DC. I am so glad I came and the staff are so kind with alot of advice for a new comer so I didn't feel lost. I will be returning with my mother in law because that is just the right place to make an impression and they have another hidden gem next door....you better ask somebody

Cecil's steakhouse and Minton's Jazz club are unparalleled. The staff is fantastic, the martini was perfectly made, the calamari with jalapeños was excellent and after walking through the kitchen and ending up in the jazz club I had the fish tacos which were absolutely delicious. That night JC Hopkins Biggish Band was fantastic, brilliant singers who could sing anything including scat. The service is phenomenal. If you're looking for wonderful entertainment, excellent food, and a one-of-a-kind New York experience this is the place to be.
Good food , nice decor and music. Came here for a birthday dinner with a large party and they were friendly and accommodating. They forgot to do the cake but overall it was a good experience.

Went with my wife and another couple,good friends on June22. Had great seats. The service was a excellent and attentive. The food was very good as were the drinks. Best of all, the Band was fabulous,as were the two singers. Had such a good time that we stayed for the second set. Will be back

The staff is nice but this place is super small. Bought my dad here for his birthday he loves live jazz but his walker couldn't fit and had to leave. Overall this place is ok for small groups and drinks.

What a great place for dinner and live jazz band and some dancing.

Food is amazing! Their fish dishes are so good, I'll have to be back to try their meat dishes. If you are going to have dessert, I recommend getting the pre-fixe 3 course meal as it's a good deal at $49. 

As I was writing this Yelp review, they were clearing for 2nd set. 1-star deducted for below.

The live band I went to was $20 admission plus minimum $30/pp for 1 hour. They have 2 sessions. I only went there because it was my favorite band. I was told I could stay for both sessions when I asked the manager upon arriving. However, during the break, the waiter asked me to pay another $20 admission to stay for the second set even though I told him that it was discussed that I could stay for the 2nd set. He did not give me any other alternative than to pay the $20 in order to stay. So I was going to leave. The manager did clear it up and let me stay though. How much food can 1 person eat?? I already packed my 2 item minimum ($30/pp/session) from the first set that I couldn't finish eating and had my beer, which was $7/beer. So for 1 hr, spending about $80 including tax and tip is a bit pricey. I would rather just give that to the band.

The first time I went the two ladies behind the bar were friendly and welcoming and were super nice. This time it was all men servers, although I did not sit at the bar this time. I felt like they embarrassed me and tried to make me feel like a cheapskate. $70 for 1hr on a Wednesday night in a half empty restaurant is not enough to try to keep a customer happy?? Wow. Will not recommend.

I was more than shocked at the behavior of this supposedly well known; " Once upon a time in Harlem" establishment. I reserve a time  slot for dinner and their show, to only find out there was no show or slot time for me and wife to sit down and eat. Lucky for me I printed out the reservation; Had I not printed it out they would've  tried to convince me that my name was not Anthony. There was no apology, no commentary coupon or anything given for this failure on their part. They even tried to hold my wife and I hostage until their 7.30 show while making their best effort at trying to convince us that it was Cecil's Place my reservation was for...this is with the printed receipt from their website showing reservations at Minton's in their hands. This place is full of shit and your damn fool to go there.  Their error spoil my entire weekend , which happen to had been my Birthday.  If your a FOOL with money then Minton is the place to go. O' By the way our reservation were for 6/8 at 5:45 pm. We were told, with them looking at the reservation that Minton closes at 5pm. There was never any kind of consideration for accountability for their error. DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY
Great place t listen to live jazz band. Food is good. They have a special in 3 course which is not bad. Will come back.

I had a great meal and the entertainment was amazing. Weird thing was the owner of the place was being loud and annoying during the performance. He was sitting at a table with about five other people. Another guest got up and asked him to be quiet so the entertainers could perform but he and his table guests kept being noisy. So the food and entertainment is great. The owner is obnoxious.

Great spot for some live Jazz, good food, drinks and that Harlem City vibe! Minus one star for the inconsistent wait staff, from changing waiters, to forgetting one of our food orders, and drink orders. Menu has a great selection, food is filling, and tasty.

I've had the pleasure of attending this lovely jazz club a little over a year ago and it was definitely a classy and fine dining experience. I came to support the jazz band playing that night, and ordered a soda and fries. I'm not a jazz lover, but I love going to jazz clubs, the vibe is always right, and I always feel like I'm in a Sex and the city episode. This is the type of place Carrie Bradshaw would bring her three girls, or most likely Mr. Big, on  date night. (If you don't get the references you are in the wrong city.)

For anyone looking for an authentic jazz club where they can have a nice family dinner, or just have a chill night out with the gals or some friends and groove to a little smooth music, this is the place for you.
Great food, music, and service. It seems like the kitchen has trouble keeping up with orders during the shows, but I've found that it's easy to make peace with that while listening to the band. =)
My credit card was charged even though I cancelled a reservation weeks in advance. That's $50, stolen!@ I've tried contacting them over the phone and by email, to no avail!! Crooked institution!!!

I went to see my friend's band as a guest.  The first thing that happened was I was harassed and embarrassed by the hostess as to my status as a guest.  She said she had no knowledge of any guest list and this had to be straightened out by the band's manager.  Then the bartender starts in on my husband huffing and puffing when we order our club sodas - we are not big drinkers - and as to whether or not he intends to pay his music charge!  Which we had every intention of paying as we had only one comp.  
Minton's!  Get your act together to be welcoming and friendly to your guests!  The attitude of the staff ruined the whole experience and vibe. 
It's no wonder the place was 1/2 empty on a Friday night.  I will be hard pressed to ever visit your establishment again. Which is a shame, as I like to support my neighborhood establishments and my fellow musicians.

Came here with my girlfriend on Saturday night for live music. We didn't make reservation and we arrived at around 9:30pm. It was only 80% full. I guess some customers already finished dinner and left. We love the atmosphere and the live Jmusic. It's $20 music charge and minimum two orders per person. Overall, we had a great night.

My experience was related to the NYE event. I don't think because of this an accurate review can be given. I want to begin with mentioning The food and music. Which I thoroughly enjoyed. This is the reason I would return which I hope to do. 
The reason for 4 stars were events leading to the food and jazz. I received an email after paying for the event (there were 4 of us) informing me there was a problem with my reservation. I called and they were unaware of the problem. After several calls in relation to this. All made by me as they didn't follow up/return call as they told me. 
We arrived with trepidation still not confident my reservation would of been received. 
It was raining and after taking our coats at coat check we were told we could not stay. Which was fine it was more the attitude. Anyway we have a drink return and we're to be taken to two seats of two. When establishing why this was so were told many people book in advance for this(agreed). He had a strategy for assigning the seats. Well in doing so I guess my strategy should have been to ask for the 4 of us to sit together. Once seats reassigned, hopefully without too much inconvenience to the other guests we had a great night. The maitre d' did offer a complementary drink. 
Verdict:
Walk in I am convinced not be a problem
Reservation be very specific about your seating. 
You will have a great time after this.

Music came on about 9:45 on a Saturday and was over by 11:15. One set but nice variety of slower, voice, and full instrumental. Band of 8 really performed well and were probably worth the cover of $20 - just wish the set was longer or they came back for a shorter set after a break. 

The food was actually surprisingly good. I didn't expect much from the food as the music was the main enticement, but reasonably priced steaks at about $40-45 and pasta $18-22. Prixe fox available for $45ish with starter, entree, and dessert. Wine typical $14 for glass and cocktails same price. Beer selection was some of the worst I've ever seen and really influenced my night as no ipa or even pale ale available. But my porterhouse was cooked perfect medium rare and was quite large. I subbed out my sides for green beans and broccoli, though was a little confused as the original dish came with potato, artichoke, and mushroom, so I took a demotion from 3 to 2 sides  didn't think that was very cool but I made the fight choice as broccoli was large portion and had a nice garlics flavor to them to perfectly compliment the steak. Green beans came smaller portioned and thin variety but again nice marination and good side. 

I'd say Minton's will provide a very nice outing for a date or family/friends gathering. Great music and affordable steak house food. The reservation policy is barely honored and we had to wait 30 minutes before seating, with poor structure of building so we were in the way of hostess and coat room, but after that mayhem, we were treated to a nice dinner and show with no complaints to add.
I love this place more every time I come here. The staff is very attentive and very congenial. The presentation of the food and drinks is wonderful. And the best live shows.

Overall the place was great, however the waitress was horrible. It took an hour for her to come back to us, and that was because I had to go and find her. I wouldnt say she is a reflection of the venue as a whole though. Still a great evening spot and would highly recommend.

Went here for dinner and live jazz on a Saturday night recently and had a wonderful time. Be sure to make a reservation as the place definitely gets packed. Plus, if you want the live jazz portion with dinner, you have two times to choose from -- 7:30 p.m. and 9:30 p.m. You will have an automatic $20 per head charge for the live jazz and dinner so keep that in mind.

Before the performance, there was a video about the history of Minton's and how the many Jazz greats had played there once upon a time. I personally enjoyed that. And the performance of course was wonderful -- the band plays for about an hour or so.

Had two cocktails that were great -- I don't remember their names but one had mezcal and the other, a Woodford Reserve, and they were both really good. Also had oysters and they were fantastic here -- got half a dozen and wish we had got a dozen. For the main course, I had the paella which was really good. The menu is pretty expansive though -- so you will find something you like.

All in all, a good time for solo, small, and large parties.

Fabulous venue in the heart of Harlem, presenting great music and ambiance.
A long bar greets the public and then come the tables. We had reservations for a party of nine. Two more friends came, so they set a long table for us.
There is a cover and two items food/drink consumption.

Most of us ordered Sangria(red). I didn't like it. Tasted like it had guava. Others had Martinis. Mixed drinks.

We ordered appetizers(Beef Empanadas, Crab Cakes, Calamari). Entrees: Ella & Louie Chicken, Mussels, Hamburger. Sides: Garlic Spinach, Sweet Potatoes, Sweet Plantains.
We sort of shared so we could have a taste.
The Beef Empanadas were very good, with a Chimichurri sauce and a salad of kale, corn, little tomatoes and avocado. 
Crab cake was delicious as well.
The Chicken has capers and a light lemons sauce it was ok.
The Mussel were very nice in a tomato broth.
Sweet Plantains divine!

Melvis Santa & Ashedí we're playing. We had to get up and dance.

DO NOT SUPPORT THIS ESTABLISHMENT!!

They do not pay their musicians. Be aware that of your $20 cover charge, none of it is going to the musicians.

Sibling night out and my lil brother chose Mintons. I went in with no big expectations after reading the reviews first. I honestly would give this place 3.5 stars.

Ambience- 5/5
Food- 2.5/5
Performances- 3.5/5
Service- 5/5

Now let me break it all down to you as short and seert as I can. When I walked in I was glad I got all dolled up. The set up is gorgeous. You'll feel out of place if you dont. 

We all sampled each other food- spinach was terribly salty, asparagus could of been bigger in size.... skimpy looking pieces.... mac and cheese wasnt bad in taste but kinda watery for my liking.... lobster ravioli was quite tasty..... t bone steak was a bit too well so made it kinda tough to chew.... garlic mash was decent. I had the drink with titos which was nice. Overall the food needs work and for the price we paid I wasnt satisfied. 

On to the performers- the saxophone guy was great. He and the piano player stole the show for me. The singer carmen was very entertaining eve. Though she kept forgetting the lyrics to songs. Some notes were off key but thats what happens when the brown liquor takes control of you.... i should know smh

Now our waiter was excellent. Answered my numerous questions and took all the pics I needed.

Will I be back? I believe so but just for appetizers, a drink and for the entertainment. 

Almost forgot about the appetizers. Enjoyed the mussels and calamari

Went for the first time on a date recently and this is the place if you want an intimate jazz experience.  The sitting is very personal, which works for dates, and the rotating jazz bands keeps the music new and refreshing.  The food is pretty good too.  I'd recommend either the Pan Seared Salmon or the Lobster Ravioli, both are great.  

I'm definitely looking forward to return visits on future dates or just solo nights out for drinks and jazz.  

Be warned though, the bill can get kinda high depending on the group that is playing.

Last night I proposed to my (now) fiancé at Minton's, and I couldn't be happier. They arranged for the band to play our song, sat us at the best table, gave us champagne with tons of congratulations and well wishing. These guys were perfect! I will always be grateful for the moment you helped fulfill. Thank you. 
I will also recommend to anyone who loves jazz or just wants to change things up to go check them out. Great music, great service, unpretentious, and so welcoming. We have our new place!!
Amazing ambiance with jazz band. Main courses that we had were delicious, however the beef skewer as appetizer was disappointing. Great restaurant for a date night.

This is one of the nicest venues for great food and jazz in NYC and a regular haunt for my friends and I. Chill atmosphere, wonderful service and really good food and cocktails. Unlike most of the local jazz spots, you're not crammed together like sardines in a can!  Definitely a big plus!

This place was amazing. I took my father there for his birthday and that was my first time going there. I love the live band that played on Saturday night. The drinks were good. The food was just absolutely amazing. So much flavor and very beautiful. My dad stepmom and I are had the chicken plate that was on the special menu. My hubby had the skirt steak. Everything was great. Oh when I forgot to mention the muscles that we had for appetizers I will definitely be returning again soon

A beautiful spot for jazz. You have room to move around, not like some places in Midtown. Lovely ambiance. Good food and friendly staff.

This was my first time here. I am looking forward to a return visit. The band is great. I met some repeat customers that go to Minton's on a regular basis.

I had a great and fun night out here. The band was great! The music was great!

Had a great time at Minton's on a Friday night. Well-attended but not quite full.  Service was friendly, professional, thorough.  Food was delivered delightfully.  Had the T-bone w grilled shrimp, side of mashed potatoes seasoned with garlic and thyme.  For dessert, cheesecake drizzled with caramel and creme on the side.  Great music featuring the Davis Whitfield Quartet.  Great evening.  Worth your time and visit!
Minton's was an absolute treat. The food was fantastic, and the music was even better. Service was good as well. It's pricey, but well worth it. I'd return.
Good atmosphere, service, and food. The staff also gets involved with the act. Maybe the only drawback is that the place is not as quaint and intimate as you would hope a jazz club to be.

I used OpenTable to book dinner at Minton's Playhouse for the evening of Memorial Day. I called the restaurant the day before to confirm the reservation. However, I woke up on Memorial Day to an email saying that the restaurant had canceled my reservation with no explanation whatsoever. I called the restaurant and they said they were closed that day. There was no apology, even when I asked why they had not called to let me know. Even AFTER this phone conversation, the restaurant's website still indicated that there would be a show that evening. Very unhappy with customer service.

I like small, quaint easy destinations.  It would be better if a valet could be established across the street.  The music is hit and miss, it's a wonder because there are a lot of starving musicians.  Last night was charming.  I like the Cecil kitchen.  So glad change came to Harlem.

I visited twice in December 2017 after not being to a Jazz club or in Harlem for quite some time. My 82-year old mother loves Christmas music and saw an ad in one of the local jazz magazines. she asked to go with my husband and I to celebrate her birthday. 
Glad we went! First, the club is beautiful! First time coming back to Mintons since I think the 90s. BIG difference! We saw the Christmas show with Brandon Bains and I enjoyed it. The guy in the bow-tie ROCKED! OMG!  and the young lady was so sweet and had an amazing voice. 
The food was great. LOVED the short ribs and the music. I read an earlier review about the sound being not so great. To each his own. But I didn't expect the highlight to be dancing at Minton's and I had a ball. My Mom even got on the dance floor! Most of the club danced too. There was some sound issues in the beginning but it got better. 
I was happy my mom had so much fun hearing the music she grew up on! especially the Calypso from Brandon. I havent heard that music since i was a kid. We came back for another Christmas show days later that was also fun. 
Coming back to NY in July and will def. go to Minton's.
Great food. Excellent service. Comfortable seating and good musical artists.

We came for our anniversary dinner on a Friday night at 6:45 and the place was surprisingly not packed (maybe people were still recovering from Valentine's Day) but ambiance was great, very romantic and elegant without feeling stuffy or pretentious. The waitstaff was amazing. Everyone was super friendly and personable, from the hostess to the gentlemen pouring our water. And it was a young staff too, very professional and had great recommendations for food. We had the restaurant week prixe fix, which came with appetizer, entree and dessert. I got the salad (delicious), skirt steak  (perfectly cooked though I wouldn't have been upset if it was slightly bigger) with asparagus and garlic mashed potatoes (buttery and delicious but not garlicky enough for me), and the tres leches (tasty but a tad on the sweet side). My fiancé got the empanadas (very tasty, I wish we had more), the salmon with grilled shrimp (cooked to perfection, perfect seasoning and best value in my opinion) and the brownie a la mode (warm, gooey and delicious, wish I ordered it). All in all a great value for $42 prixe fix price. Live jazz music was great. $15 cover added to your bill but totally worth it and a much better value than some of the seedier jazz bars with higher covers and not as nice ambiance. This is a great place for dates or special occasions and the food is very good, but the music made it taste better. Would definitely go back again.

Decent band, friendly (but slow) service, bad drinks (my dates whiskey was watered down and my dirty martini was subpar-tasted like dish water)and amazing company! Upon checking out charged a $15/per person music fee (although we asked upon arrival if this was waived since we had dinner at the Cecil..we were told it would be waived..by the manager). Had a great dinner at Cecil's prior (they share the same kitchen) and came here for a nightcap and some music....disappointed!

The strip steak came out and I laughed so hard that I literally cried LOL. The salmon was pretty good but the overall food portions were ridiculous for what we were charged. Where are we eating when we leave here??? I had a headache when I left smh. Never, ever, ever again.

This is for Sunday jazz brunch. I'm sad to give a negative review because the food and jazz were great but we the service was so terrible. After being seated, we were ignored for 30 minutes and had to flag down a waiter to order. We noticed people who arrived at the same time were almost done eating and we still didn't have our food. Finally, we flagged down our waiter again (seriously, not once did he come up to us during the whole meal) - our food came almost immediately after that (it was cold since he obviously forgot to give it to us). He was just rude and didn't seem to care. They also gave us the wrong order for 2 out of 3 orders. One was much more expensive than what we wanted. After we politely told them, they were not apologetic and proceeded to give us the wrong order AGAIN. At this point after waiting so long, we just asked for the check. They messed up again and overcharged us so we had to flag them down again. It was just one mistake after another, long waits and no apologies. We will not be going back.

This place is sad. The music was great but they overcharge for everything, nickel and dime you and the food is cold and bland. Management is very rude and I watched the owner/manager treat the employees and musicians like dirt. I would highly suggest looking elsewhere. There's plenty of other great spots for music and food in that neighborhood.

We came for the early set featuring Brandon Bain. I'll start on the high notes. The service was pretty great (although the bar service was slow). The door and wait staff were friendly and attentive. The decor is also great, modern, with a touch of nostalgia. The lighting at the bar is kind of dreadful, and the lights on the left row of banquets are too bright. Ask to sit on the right, unless you want to be spotlighted the whole evening. 

The food was mediocre. We both ordered steaks. They weren't particularly flavorful, and the plating left us wondering if the kitchen was running out of food. Very meager portions, especially for the price. The tiramisu was missing the booze. The oysters, on the other hand, were delicious. 

Finally, the music was really a disappointment. The sound balance was dreadful. Brandon Bain's vocals struggled to be on key and were too loud and overly present. Meanwhile, the fantastic band seemed to sound a million miles away. I appreciated the intention of the holiday show, but the program was all off, and in any case, the settings were either too ambitious for Bain's voice, or he was fully out of his element. The Banana Boat song was neither apropos, nor executed well enough to forgive. The ensuing conga line was overly contrived and not in the least entertaining.  

I wanted to leave the minute my dinner was finished, but of course I'd paid $10 on top of a too-expensive dinner to be there, so I waited it out like an A-train delay due to signal malfunctions at 118th Street.

The jazz steal the show. Don't go with a chatty person because this place is for listening. Food is ok. Great bar, cozy, chic, elegant. I suggest this place for special occasions and jazz lovers. Don't bring your bad kids.

This sounds improbable but it really happened. Six of us made reservations for 8 o'clock but we're not told that Music start at 7:30 and 930. We waited 45 minutes to be seated and our very nice waiter took our orders right away so that the food would be in quickly. At 10 o'clock still no food and other tables that we're seated after us had finished Dinner.When we asked what is going on we were told that the kitchen is shared with their sister restaurant and they had no control over when the food will come out. After ordering drinks and waiting some more We were told four times the food will come out in 10 minutes,we got up and walked out $200 later for music that we only listen to half the program and still no food. We were told sorry with a smile and that was it. Wow what a way to run a railroad. We are still hungry.

In full transparency this a review for Cecil's, and their manager/s. Last year, my now spouse and I got married at a local garden that we volunteer with. We dined at Cecil's with our family, a group of around 10. We had the chef's tasting menu which was amazing, a variety of different dishes, the oxtail dumplings, fish, wagyu burger, cinnamon hens, etc. etc. everything was out promptly. They succeeded in wowing a motley group of people with wildly different tastes and cultural food heritages. Cut to a year later, felt some nostalgia, especially considering the restaurant was closed for renovations, my husband emailed asking for a menu. They responded promptly and scrounged up a menu for our wedding album.

I so appreciate their responsiveness, and the memorable dinner we had there.

So much fun! We happened to come in the first few days that Minton's re-opened but based on the crowd you would never know it had been closed down.

The reservations are based on set show times here, so if you're coming to eat, its best to make a reservation for the 9:30 show which seats for dinner around 830.  If you come for the earlier show you will have to give up your table for the second seating - which sucks because then you miss out on any surprise jam sessions.

They were serving a sample menu from the Cecil - which was delicious.  The place is very small and intimate - just what you would want from a jazz club.  I am by no means a jazz buff, and I still loved the music.  The crowd was also a great mix - another aspect that really added to the overall ambiance... I can't wait to go back!!
Unique and fun at this jazz club eatery. Went to see a special burlesque show that was pretty darn good. Jazz nights are great too and so is the food- hearty and comforting. Best Sunday brunch award!

FYI - great place for ambience, food and drinks in my several visits here.  Please note that they're undergoing renovations in summer 2017 and due to reopen at a date TBD as of this writing (Aug 2017).  Looks like this'll also be accompanied by their adjoining sibling restaurant (The Cecil) reopening as a steakhouse --- should be many interesting and fun meals ahead at both places!

The Jazz and Blues place to go in Harlem. The music is better than anything for sure. The drinks and food items are very good as well. It will be an experience you will want to repeat frequently. I highly recommend it.
Service was horrible. Sat for 20 min at the bar and no one greeted me. Food is over priced with small portions. Music was great!!!

Great spot! Came here with some friends for brunch. 

They have  live music on weekends, really nice jazz. I believe for dinner there is a cover charge for live music, but don't let that deter you.

I suggest making a reservation as the place isn't huge. For brunch there's a pre-fix menu option which is a great deal.

Food: Try the mac&cheese, kale salad or smoked pork ribs. All great options.

The staff is super friendly and attentive. Overall, great place to listen to some music and enjoy the company of good friends.

Minton's is such a special place. To have the opportunity to sit so close to wildly talented musicians, while enjoying their awesome food, is a real treat. Service is also impeccable, and the cocktails are lots of fun. I have to also shout out to their lovely reservations team, whose folks couldn't have been nicer as I juggled timing and guest count against delayed flights of out of towners.

Loved that Minton's n the Cecil merged!  Had dinner on a Sunday with a large group and enjoyed delicious, creative food while listening to live jazz.  Food was the highlight.  Chicken wings n biscuits were delicious.  Loved the prawn dish and the collard salad.  Definitely check this place out some the merger!

Went last Sunday for brunch at Minton's and left feeling underwhelmed with the food.
Came with a party of 4 about 30 minutes before the live music started. 2 of us did the pre fixe menu which includes a small plate, entree, and drink.

"African-Asian" cuisine - I could definitely taste the fusion with the smoked pork ribs I ordered. Very tender and full of flavor (would order again) 
Also ordered the mac and cheese (pretty disappointed if you can see from the picture was definitely lacking in flavor and cheesiness).

Two of my friends ordered the chicken wings and pancake- the wings got good reviews- crispy and not too dry.
But the pancakes were definitely dry and very dense. Had to ask the waiter for more maple syrup.

I ordered this black bean and oxtail mixture toast with two eggs on top (not mentioned in their current brunch menu but see picture below) 
- the first time they brought it out the toast was visibly burnt and had to ask the waiter to take it back because it was an overwhelming charcoal flavor.
Second time around, it was much better! Generous chunks of oxtail but overwhelming about of means- the bread was quite good and moist. Flavor tho...was lacking.
Ordered a mimosa and a Bloody Mary- both okay.

4 stars for attentiveness of waiter
5 starts for the live music ( seriously awesome) 
4 stars for Ambiance (really nice interior) 
3 stars for food.

Wasn't a terrible experience- the great service and music were much appreciated but the food mediocre.

On our way out we were handed a box with two truffles- so it did end on a sweet note.

Overall 3.5
Everything is so flavorful! Great service, and beautiful atmosphere. I've been here a few times and every time I wonder why I don't go more often. A gem.
This place is amazing, the music is great.  Must go for Saturday​ or Sunday brunch.  Chicken and pancakes is a must and the kale salad

It was just okay.

I came here for a mother's day brunch and immediately fell in love with the decor. Once you step inside you feel like you're almost transported into the space. It's intimate, dimly lit, autographs from jazz musicians accent the wall and there's a live band playing towards the end. Service was fine, but nothing special. We ordered the brunch prix-fixe. I had the collard green salad, which was favorful but again, nothing special. I did try some of the mac and cheese and that was pretty good. For the entree I had the smothered chicken and grits, which was good but a very heavy dish, and I thought the grits were a little soupy.
A wonderful place to enjoy live music and company with friends. A great alternative to a night club if you just want to hang out.

A great place for brunch! Wonderful even though it's a bit uptown. Great that we just had normal brunch prices even though there was a wonderful jazz performance! I was surprised the place wasn't super packed on Easter brunch. They offer a great prix fix menu- appetizers were large in size. The entrees were a little greasy for my taste, but the leftovers were delicious. Delicious mac n cheese, most of all!

Minton's! What a special Harlem jewel it turned out to be last Sat. 4/22/17. 
I was one of the coordinators of a surprise party event & it was a spectacular hit not only because of the sumptuous brunch that we were served, or the fabulous live jazz band music that tickled our souls, but because of the extra special care that we were given by the staff. Shout outs to Rosa & Vonda and to our fabulous servers. Everyone seemed to go that extra  step to make sure that all our needs were met, and that we had the terrific time we had hoped to. They did not disappoint! They were well staffed, and the beautiful decor was warm & inviting as well as intimate. I would highly recommend that you consider Minton's for your next party event!

Four of us went to the Saturday Brunch on April 15th. We all ordered a brunch combo that comes with 2 selections and a cocktail. The food was pretty good. The band and a singer did 2 sets which is fine, but we were seated in the very front which made it hard to converse.

I would recommend this restaurant because the price for the meal and entertainment was a good value.

Went to Minton's today for Palm
Sunday Brunch. The food was great, but the service only so, so. We had a 1:45 reservation, but decided to go earlier to see if we could get in. It turns out the hostess with the mostess said we could. My friend went in, while I waited in the car. He told her we were going to parking. It too us longer than expected to park, since parking is at a premium on Sunday (especially Palm Sunday). By the time we got back, she'd given our table away & told us to sit at the bar until she figured it out. Mind you we still had a 1:45 reservation. What bothered us is that she didn't call us (she had our #) or try to accommodate us in a timely fashion once we got back. Finally after sitting at the bar for at least 20 mins, she came over & said you see all these people, I'll work on a table for you once they've all been seated. These people came in after us. I told her we'd eat at the bar at that point. She said go right ahead in a sarcastic way. Luckily for us, the bartender Jorge was super friendly. He went out his way to ensure our experience & meal was worth the wait! My advice to the management is to get rid of the negative woman who was hostess if you don't want to loose business.

I came here without reservations. I attempted to have dinner here during restaurant week with a friend, but couldn't because it was all booked. However I was allowed to sit at the bar, I had the Fruit De La passion drink which was oh so good. As I waited for me friend to arrive, I was able to see some of the performance that was going on. Also the bartenders as well as the patrons were very nice and easy to talk to. For those reasons I couldn't rate any less.

My husband and I went to Minton's for Valentine's Day looking for good food and good music. We got both. The band playing, The Willerm Delisfort Project, was transcendent. It was some of the best jazz I've heard in the city. I would say the music definitely outshone the food, but I was OK with it. I would definitely go back for jazz and drinks.
I had brunch here yesterday with my girlfriend and the food was amazing and the entertainment. Jazz band was great, I will definitely return to Minton's.

I was hoping for more.

The live music was exceptional. Great ambiance, a bit small you're practically sitting with the party next to you.

Fast Company recommended "The Cecil" and I was excited for the Asian-African fusion. When I heard they merged with Minton's I wasn't sure. Changing ownership and all that, changes everything and the food was sub-par, the service, disappointing. 

The music and the charisma from the bartenders and manager made up for what was lacking.

I'd go again for the music and drinks at the bar.

We had a great Friday date night here! Cool and eclectic live band (we were surprised to learn $10/person would be added to our bill for each set, but totally fair and worth it) and good food. For apps we got the seafood basket (not great, skip!), the oxtail dumplings (good, try!) and for entrees I got the Jambalaya (interesting but not mind blowing) and beau got the porterhouse (good, try!). Food was tasty but our server left a LOT to be desired. I'll skip the details since the manager made it right when we complained. The restaurant is super tiny so strongly advise making a reservation on a Thursday or Friday night. Drinks are a little pricey...wine, however was decent and delish.

First let me start off by saying I went to Minton's this Sunday, Feb 26th for my cousins birthday celebration. She wanted a place that had great food, live jazz and a fun atmosphere. Our party was large as we had 16 people. The live jazz by Dandy Wellington was great, the band phenomenal, he was personable, an excellent host and jazz singer. I truly enjoyed all of their sets. He was even kind enough to take a picture with my cousin for her birthday. 
Unfortunately, the food was not good at all. Each of us agreed that the atmosphere was lovable, jazz music phenomenal but the only person out of 16 who enjoyed their dish was the person who ordered the Grilled Wagyu Burger. Although, the brunch sounds appetizing it was everything but that. For appetizers we tried the macaroni and cheese which was over powered by the taste and smell of onions, the kale salad was lack luster and the smoked pork ribs were a hit or miss, some of our guests said it was good others said it was horrible. As an entree I ordered the country breakfast which was over powered by scallions, many people ordered the chicken and waffles which was horrible. Most of our party sent the chicken back since it looked dry and very dark, the plantain waffle was dry and burnt around the edges. 
We didnt want to do too much complaining because it was my cousins birthday. However as waitress if you see that almost all of the food of your patrons is left on the plate you may want to inquire what the issue is. All and all we wanted to love this place but couldn't especially since the horrible food and lack luster drinks equated to $57 per person and when our waitress brought us back the check saying we were short $10 (she received $121 gratuity although besides taking our order we rarely saw her). She was indeed wrong and instead of apologizing responded by saying I'm not good with math. I'm sure this would be a great spot to here music but I don't recommend the food or bringing a large party. Sorry I wanted to love this place sooo bad :(

In an effort to find some great places that the locals love, we made our way uptown to Minton's.  First of all, from downtown take the 2 train to 116th Street, then walk a couple of short blocks.
Reservations really helped. We got there a bit late, but called on the way.  Sam was super! She was able to get us in, and didn't make us feel bad for mixing up our trains.   

OK. So, we get seated, and were happily greeted by Mimi, who brought us the good news in the form of a drinks menu.  Their wine list, by the glass, is somehow concise, and still varied.  I'm finicky about such things, yet still found some fine wines from which to chose.  Our friend had to have his daily soother, and claims that they made him a very fine "Old Fashioned".  He looked soothed.

Mimi guided us through the appetizer choices, though she couldn't think of one that might be a miss.  We decided to share an order of the Crispy Chicken Wings, which were meaty, sticky and delicious!  We also split and order of the Short Rib Toast, which was moist and rich, and satisfying.  For our entrée two of us had the Gumbo.  Now, this is not your typical Louisiana Gumbo.  It was a more delicate, slightly spicy, richer gumbo.  It seemed to have more of the African influence that Creole food has to offer.  Wonderful!  The portion looked, to my hungry eyes, to be less than I wanted, but it was the perfect amount in that it left juuuust enough room for a share of dessert. Our other guest had the Roasted Chicken which, when it arrived, was the last we heard from him.  He lavished in the chicken, adding little to the conversation save an occasional low moan of satisfaction.  We each got a taste of it (for scientific purposes, of course) and quickly knew why he hardly spoke.  This chicken leaves you speechless.  It is glazed, as Mimi described, with a savory mix of spices light enough not to hid the flavor of the chicken, but still remind you that you are among culinary genius. 

Live Jazz! Great Food! Carrot Cake! Yum!

Make sure you call a couple days in advance to know if they're going to be charging a music fee and when the set times are going to be at! We called 1.5 weeks in advance when we made the reservation and were told that there would be none, but to our surprise when we arrived it was $10/person. That would have been okay, but it ended up being 20 mins of music while the band was on break in between sets the rest of our dinner. 

Initially came here for NYC Restaurant Week, but then we ended up just ordering from the regular menu. Service and food was really good, but it wasn't necessarily worth the price. 

Pros: okra fries and the steak
Cons: oxtail dumplings (and that music charge again)

The service was outstanding. Really friendly and welcoming. The shrimp basket was pretty good. I got the steak (I know I know) that was really overcooked and slightly burnt. (medium well)
Really nice ambiance but probably wouldn't come back when I'm back in town.

I was here in 2/16/17 for an intimate dinner with a friend for his birthday.  Upon arriving for our 715pm reservation we were greeted by the host and informed that there would be a 20 min wait because our waitress was working several tables and wanted to catch up on service. No a good start, so we sat at the bar and go a drink and waited.  Upon being seated we were greeted by Melinda, who I might add is an AWESOME waitress.  She offered up water and asked if we had questions about the menu.  She was back in a flash to take our order.  The appitizers came out in due time and were delicious.  We had the Oxtail Dumplings and Homemade Biscuits with Chickpea Puree'.  Upon completion the table was cleaned and dinner served.  Melinda also gave the birthday boy a free glass of champange for his birthday and greeted him by name, since I put that on the reservation request.  The food was delicious and the jazz ensemble was always great.  Because the biscuits was kinda hard and the 20 min wait when we arrived on time for the reservation is the only reason I deducted a star.  I am sure I will make another trip in the near future.

I had a great dinner here last Friday for an early valentine's/restaurant week combo.  The food was incredible.  I had the short rib toast, chicken, and chocolate cake, and my boyfriend had the same but with the chicken mousse/cornbread.  We split the biscuits to start.  Everything was absolutely amazing.  I think my favorite was the short rib toast.  Also, the portion size was huge...a little too big for me to even finish. Drinks were also good.

The music was phenomenal.  I guess that shouldn't be a surprise, since all the greats played at Minton's, but it's nice to know the quality is still really important.  Quick note, on Friday and Saturday nights there's a $10 cover per person for music (even if you're eating dinner).  

The only sort of downside was that because we were seated next to the band, we couldn't really talk.  Then again, we got to appreciate the music even more.

I've had an amazing brunch a few times at The Cecil and was disappointed to hear they were merging kitchens with Minton's but hoped the food would survive. I was disappointed. 

For starters, I am a VIP Open Table guest yet I was asked to use a credit card to hold my table. Annoying but I understand patrons are fickle these days and the restaurant business is tough. 

I arrived exactly at my reservation time and found the host table empty. He finally emerged with such a poor attitude I knew I was in for a rough afternoon. He ignored me to seat some people waiting at the bar, checked their coats, returned their tickets all at a snails pace. Finally I was seated at 1:10pm. 

My friend ordered the chicken and waffles (which indicates a plantain waffle) and I had the pre-fix starting with the mac & cheese and then getting the chicken biscuit. 

My friends dish arrived without syrup. The time it took to flag down the one waitress for syrup her waffle began loosing heat. In addition, upon tasting her meal it was evident the waffle had no plantain in it. I am Cuban. I know what plantains taste like. My mac & cheese was the only tasty thing I ate. The chicken biscuit was so tiny it would not cover the palm of my hand. The biscuit was dry and hard and the chicken sausage was luke warm. The side of sweet potato hash was undercooked. Potatoes should easily be eaten with a fork and these were too hard! We suffered through the meal both deciding on our next brunch we'll head downtown despite living 3 blocks from Mintons. Never again.

Excellent tasting food and jazzy atmosphere.  We absolutely love Chef JJ's (Joe) food.  The african asian flavors were out of this world.  Our meals were extremely tasteful.  Everything was so good.  I went with a group of 6 and we each enjoyed our meals.  Can't wait to return when we visit NY again.  My friends said Minton's is definitely a must.   Jazz band was awesome as well.

Loved this place! Tasty food, good drinks, and a great band. We were there in Friday night celebrating my daughter's 23rd birthday- make a reservation, it's a busy place. All of the tables have a good view of the band and people are very friendly. I recommend the steak and ALL of the appetizers. I can't wait to go back.

This was listed as a top 5 restaurant week choice and I know why. You get tasty food and a live show all for great price in a jazz supper club.  Had a fantastic time.

Champagne 

Appetizers are all big enough to share!
Collard greens salad- not sure how they made this but I loved it! 
Chicken liver- very tasty!

Lamb- very good
Fish- so so good!

Dessert
Gotta go check this place out! Lovely ambience, great food, great jazz and historical spot. Diverse crowd, safe, easy to find and great service! Keep Harlem rockin!

Really great comfort food and awesome jazz music! We went during restaurant week and the place was packed on a Wednesday. I ordered off the regular menu because I read that the crispy chicken wings were amazing, and they did not disappoint! I had the seafood gumbo to finish my meal off and it was delicious. My boyfriend ordered the Prix fixe menu- ordering the short rib toast, lamb and chocolate cake- which were all so good! They definitely were not dried out from sitting under heat lamps like you get from some places during restaurant week. Staff was all super nice and the venue is fun and lounge-y. We are already planning to go back!

We came here to enjoy the show and check out the restaurant week menu. While the ambiance is great and people were very kind, we were a bit disappointed with the quality of the food. We got our appetizer pretty quickly after we placed our order but it took another hour to get our main dish and ended up eating really late. Besides the appetizers which were excellent the main dishes were quite disappointing. Not very tasty, fish was super salty and the lamb did not taste much like lamb. Dessert was just a regular chocolate cake and there is not much other option. Nothing to do with all the other dessert pictures posted here. I guess they don't have it any more after they merged? I don't feel we got our money's worth. I would only go back for the music and drinks.

Minton's is a great mix of contemporary fusion cuisine with an old school jazz club.  Went here on a Saturday night for dinner and the live show.  We showed up early and waited at the bar for our table to be ready.  I will say this: Minton's had some of the most comfortable bar stools I have ever experienced!  My wife tried one of the signature cocktails and really enjoyed it.  However, the mark up on liquor is pretty steep ($16 for a cocktail and $15 for a single pour of Michters).

We were seated at a small table near the stage, which was excellent for taking in the show, but you definitely have to strategize about when to converse with your dining partner as the volume of the band can be a bit loud when you're that close.  But it's great if you want to zone out with your drink and vibe with the music.
