The food: overall the food was excellent! We tried the oxtail dumplings and crispy chicken wings as a first course and the gumbo and burger as our entrees.  The dumplings were well made with a subtle but interesting green apple and scallion cream sauce.  The wings were crispy sticky goodness with a nice bit of heat at the end.

The burger was served with a Vidalia onion sauce and smoked poor belly (wife loved it), and the gumbo was the perfect blend of smoke, salt, and heat, with generous chunks of shrimp, crab, and Chinese sausage throughout.  I would highly recommend pairing your gumbo with an order of the house made biscuits, which are served on a curried chickpea concoction (which was a nice bonus).

Minton's was a marvelous experience and I can't wait to go back for more!

Had dinner tonight at Minton's. The food and the service was lackluster. Our party of 8 was served food as if we were sitting at totally different tables. We arrived for a 6:30 reservation to an empty restaurant. As the night progressed the band played and finished while tables that arrived after ours sat ate and left. Once our food finally arrived, no ones food was hot. It was either luke warm/dried out. The Charred eggplant that I had, was so dry that my fork would not even go through it. I did go to this restaurant when it was the Cecil. It was so much better. The Cecil is hurting itself by joining with this joint. Awful experience.

Did you miss The Cecil? Well, don't, because they are just next door here at Minton's, their sister restaurant. The Cecil has merged together with Minton's. The same chefs, Chef Alexander Smalls and Chef JJ are still running the show serving up african asian food. Who knew this combination would be so amazing? 

After going up a short flight of stairs, a jazz supper bar vibe fills upon you as you enter. The dining atmosphere was intimate, romantic and classy at it's best. Checked in with the hostess, and got seated right away, I was crossing my fingers not to sit tightly between two tables, that didn't end so well but I rather not be a nuisance to ask for a seat change.Wine was calling out through the vibe of the restaurant. The wine list had a good variety of new world wines, italian whites, african reds etc. Felt like going with a bottle of classic sweet riesling from Germany to go with my meal. 

The Chicken Liver Mousse, In a hot skillet serves an amazing hot corn bread, topped with a good heavy portion of chicken liver pate then smeared with a sweet fruit jam, potent and delicious flavors in every single bite. Let's just say, my fork never left the dish. I do wish there was a little more bread to this though, what am I going to do with all that flavor? The four pieces oxtail dumplings came swimming in a small dish of green apple curry and a medium sized taro root chip. I was not a huge fan of this dish because of the curry. I might enjoy the dumplings with only a small dip of the curry sauce instead. Afro-Asian American Gumbo, very rich and hearty concoction of chicken, shrimp and crab then topped with a few pieces of fried okra. A bowl of Feijoada is what everyone really needs with a heavy portion of spicy black beans, lamb sausage and topped with a  piece of tender fall-off-the-bone oxtail. If you only had to choose one entree, this would be it! If you are a brussel sprouts fan, you would pretty much order them anywhere but would it be as on point as this plate of delicious goodness with bacon, pineapple and peanut, giving you a variety of taste and texture? Just do it. The Okra Fries is not like anything I have ever had, simply amazing. It is absolutely a must get because which heaven did they fry these in? For once, I actually had no room for dessert. 

I live 20 miles away from here but I would definitely be down to return again someday. Overall, it's been awhile since I had such an amazing meal and I owe it to Minton's and everyone that made the experience wonderful. 

P.S My only big con about my experience was the patrons sitting next to me. Two neatly dressed, suited, yet obnoxious guys sat next to our table was talking way too loud for me to enjoy the live music. Their conversation was definitely not kept to a simmer and that ruined my first jazz experience. They talked through my entire dining experience, the musician's performance, speech and pretty much louder than the clapping surrounding them. Not sure why they didn't just choose somewhere else to have a full-on conversation.

I have been here three times. Once for a dinner on a Friday night, the second was for a Gala and the third for yesterday for a Sunday brunch.

I have never regretted coming. The food is great. The staff is warm and inviting. The ambience is full with comfort and beauty. The artists who have performed were all amazing. I love this place, obviously - I keep coming back!

Minton's is a revived Harlem jazz club with a wonderful spirit and elegance. They have a nice varied, but compact menu of food and drinks, including a healthy selection of wines. 

All the people here are warm, courteous and friendly, and the night we came (to an early show) we heard a really good jazz quartet. The room's acoustics are intimate and the burger knocked me out. Yummmy! We're looking forward to our next visit!

I came here for a dinner date on a Friday night.  The restaurant has a very nice ambiance that allows you to be taken back to that Era, where speakeasy lounges were popular. The live band was great,  people were actually up dancing and enjoying themselves. I suspect some could've been staff to get the crowd live but some were definitely patrons. The drinks we great.  The only downfall of this place was the food. The food was not great at all. I had the fried porgy, it didn't have any seasoning on it. It was over some type a tomato based sauce with some potato textured thing. I also got the sweet plaintain waffle which was the only thing I enjoyed. My date had the pork chop. From my side of the table it looked delicious but he didn't even eat half. If you like bland food you may enjoy it, but it was not tasty at all.

Sadly we had an ugly experience, our first time patronizing Minton's.  We an African American couple arrived and sat at a table in the front near the jazz band, the music was very enjoyable, atmosphere pleasant. We were seated 15 - 20 minutes, no service. A Caucasian couple arrived and sat at a table across from us.  A waitress appeared, looked at us, but went over to the table where the Caucasian couple had just arrived. She spoke to them, walked away and returned to their table. After speaking to them again, she again turned around, looked at us and walked over to the table next to us, turned her back and proceeded to clean the table off, never saying a word to us.  We got up and asked in the front for the Manager. She was setting at the bar with customers, drunk and smelled like alcohol.  She confimed that the waitress had our section and said that she would speak to her later. We walked out, never to return.  We recommend that no people of color patronize Minton's, out right prejudice is acceptable.

Had true pleasure of dining at Minton's for my aunts 100 years Bday. The staff was extremely pleasant and the service was on point /stellar. The food is outstanding..Great spot for private parties and intimate gatherings. The Manager Q makes it happen. And my complaints to the chef.

Classy jazz spot with plenty of elbow room and mostly good food.  "Waygu" burger was delicious (flame broiled?).  Asked for medium got medium rare but still good. Good crispy fries.  My companions had Mac n Cheese, calamari (portion small) and pork chop (tasty but a tad overdone). No cover (but two item minimum) for excellent set by Teodross Avery.  And yes they seated us in the back when the place was empty but some gentle cajoling got them to move us up.

Minton's Jazz Club was an excellent experience for me!  The performance of Willie Jones III and his band was phenomenal!  I truly loved the atmosphere of Minton's because I felt like I was transported back to the time of Sir Duke,  Miss Ella and Lady Day, Billie Holiday. The wait staff was truly courteous!  The only downer was the food! Never in my experience have I had such a horrible meal.  There's not much to offer on the menu as it was and I was thoroughly disappointed!   Not sure if it was an off night for the chef because not only was my meal horrible but the couple sitting next to me complained about theirs as well. 

The next time I visit Minton's I will go to Cecil's to eat first!

At Minton's enjoying dinner and a jazz set.  The house manager, Q, is taking good care of us.  Good music, good food, great house manager!!  The menu is a new one and we are very pleased.   Nice intimate, elegant spot

This place is a hidden gem.  The atmosphere and décor is sexy and inviting...perfect for a date night!  The maître d was very pleasant and welcoming...we had a reservation at 8:30 and were immediately seated.  Our waitress was lovely...she was attentive and knowledgeable about the dishes and cocktails.  Kudos to the chef...I had the pork chops and my boo had the chicken fried chicken.  Both were delicious and the portion size required a doggie bag!  Lastly, the Mark Whitfield, Jr Trio were outstanding!!!  I'm not certain why this is the first time I've been here but I will definitely be back!!!

Obnoxious house manager refused to seat us at table reserved a while ago because "some VIPs just booked it."  Not sure who creates first and second class customers for this place. But either we didn't qualify as good enough or someone else qualified as better. This is no way to run a restaurant. 
Wouldn't recommend to anyone. We walked out.

You ruined my 50th birthday dinner. It's not bad enough that this was the first time I was to celebrate it since 9/11/2001. 

But to reserve a table for 5 and specifically have asked when I reserved that it be away from the stage and, after waiting 1/2 hour, find that the table I requested was to be given to a "last minute VIP" is disgusting. How dare you! So you treat some guests better than others.

I am a now former customer, and, you are responsible to ruining an important birthday.
Great show and good food. Enjoyed the atmosphere and people immensely. Emily Braden was wonderful as was her piano, percussionist and bass players.

The music and atmosphere was quite nice. We went there on a Friday night, expecting it to be crowded as it said on some of the reviews. To our surprise it was not busy, a lot of empty tables. No reservations needed. The band was loud but that could be because the place was not full. The food was not what we expected. My partner had meat, which was tough. I had the 1/2 chicken, which look like half of a baby Cornish hen or 1/4 of a whole chicken. The sauce had too much of an acids taste, which did not work well for that dish. They also had a sparse wine selection. No Muscat or reisling  Would not recommend for dinner. Music yes.

What a lovely surprise!  I went to Minton's on Saturday night with 2 friends to hear our fave jazz harpist, Brandee Younger.  She was great; no surprise.  The surprises came with the ambience and the menu: no longer did Minton's feel stuffy and a little pretentious and WAY overpriced (though delish), on Saturday the place was filled, the menu flexible in price and portion sizes, and it really did feel like a jazz club, not a nostalgic relic.  I'm going back again soon!

Minton's is certainly one of Harlem's Gems! Took my husband here to celebrate a promotion and we had an awesome time. Food option were a bit limited which is my reason for 4 stars but other than that I highly recommend this place for some a nice musical evening in harlem.

I love Minton's! I really, really, really, really, really, really love Minton's. It's everything I would normally stray away from when picking a venue to hang out in...but for some reason that is what makes it so awesome. Went to Minton's on a Friday night to see my friend play. The crowd is "seasoned" and the venue is "old school cool." You won't find many youngin's hanging out here. But again, that was fine. I actually really enjoyed this old school flava.  I was with 2 other friends and we decided to sit at the bar for the night. I would normally order a glass of wine at a venue like this, but it was a rough week and I needed something that packed a heavier punch. I ordered one of THE most delicious drinks I have ever had in my entire life. The name of the cocktail escapes me. The ingredients included basil, gin and agave. I ended up ordering 4 of them (don't judge me). The bartenders are the bomb. My drink was made well every single time. I ordered a side of fries to pick at and those were yummy too. Minton's is where it is at. Don't come here if you're looking to turn up and get loose. It's a laid-back spot with a hell of a lot of class.

110% perfect experience for Valentine's Day a few years back. Sat next to a few Harlem locals who had moved to Jersey and were visiting on a whim. The food was excellent, the dessert (my fave course) was divine, and the music was accompanied by dance by a famous choreographer whose name I forget unfortunately.  I had been painfully depressed that winter and this one night of authentic jazz with superb vocals lifted my spirits in ways only music and soul food can.

I am sitting in Minton's right now for the Valentine's Day brunch.
why 2 stars:
1. Waited out in the cold for them to open doors at 12:05 instead of 11. There were 10-15 of us out there and I took it upon myself to bang really loud. It worked.
2. There were supposed to be 2 sets of music for the brunch and a music charge. I've been here since 12. It is now 1:30. No music...
3. Staff should be trained on menu. Said dishes would include ingredients they they did no include. Also, stuff on menu was not available. 
4. Should be salt and pepper available on tables. Very bland food.

The waiters are very nice...they just need more training
Excellent food and fantastic music.  Atmosphere is terrific.  Not a big selection of entrees, but what we ordered (gumbo) was delicious.

Elegant beautiful setting for an intimate hearing of superb jazz with delicious food!   Staff are warm and welcoming.

We enjoyed the signature gumbo dish, with a starter terrific salad, but really flipped out over the collard greens with peanuts side. The desserts were likewise gourmet delectable - different, Southern inspired and not too sweet. We had the cobbler with biscuit crust and the pecan creation - subtle, not cloying. Oh yes, the biscuits! Don't miss those! Ahhhh! Served with whipped maple butter! A must. 

There did not appear to be a lot of weekend parking on the street, but there was a convenient parking garage on the next block.

This historic Jazz club is a delight! We plan to return again and again!
Fantastic jazz , great atmosphere , good Bloody Mary's . Good and service are excellent .

we had such a memorable experience at Mintons. the food is great but not the main attraction. the music was excellent. the ambiance was legitimately sexy. the service was attentive. i would absolutely recommend this place to anyone looking for a memorable New York dinner.

some tips:
-if youre visiting from out of town you may feel timid about going to Harlem. the area was perfectly safe and a very short walk from the subway.
-there are far more reservation opportunities if you call versus what may be online
-you can sit at the bar which still has a good view of the stage if you are traveling solo. i was uncertain if i had to make reservations for a table or not but if you plan to eat dinner it seems to be a must.
-there is a $25 charge for the music per person at the tables.
-there is no dancing but plenty of people feeling the music at their table.
-the band played for about 60% of our dinner. then the band took a break and restarted the same set. so by the time we finished dessert we had gotten the full show. 
-ignore the haters on this page. service was great. food was definitely better than average. i think this place deserves a round of applause.
This review is long overdue but the food is superb I came here back when they had the crab cake sandwich, the drinks are tasty and price is very reasonable will come again

The food here is horrible and the service is just as bad.  We were never told that the entrees were a la cart so after waiting for an eternity we were served 1 piece of chicken on a plate. Seriously? Who eats chicken without a side or even a piece of toast. The chicken itself was not seasoned and the gumbo was barely palatable.   To top things off we told there was a $25 minimum to sit at a table.  When we got the check there was an extra $15 per person surcharge for the live music. Cost is not the issue here, it is the lack of transparency and not setting the right expectations that really gets under my skin.

GOOD FOOD, EXCELLENT JAZZ, HORRIBLE SERVICE, OVER-PRICED
I went to enjoy the music of a good friend,  jazz by Barbara King & the Spirit of Jazz.  Deviled eggs & Bird cocktail were good. May have enjoyed another, or even an an entree or dessert if the waiter had ever returned to the table. Had to go looking for him when I was ready to pay.  A bit hidden, so disconcerting when walking in the neighborhood. Lastly, be aware of music coverage charge added to bill.

Came here to see a performance by a friend of a friend. We had seen her a few years back, at the no-longer-in-business and greatly-missed Lenox Lounge, and were really impressed. Minton's provides a step back into a Harlem of a different era. It's a little pricy, but not extremely so. 

We liked our fancy drinks and bottled beers (nothing on tap). I really liked the fried chicken liver appetizer. Smoked-trout deviled eggs came 2 eggs (4 half-eggs) per order, and tasted more like egg than trout. Our salad had mixed greens and roasted cherry tomatoes. They have a lot of "Low Country" food, from the coastal Carolinas. We split a seafood gumbo, and we had to try "peanut butter collard greens" made from a gullah recipe. We both thought the greens were delicious. Ask the house-made hot sauce, it's plenty hot!

Rather than dessert, we opted for another round of drinks. If you want a real "New York-y" NY experience, this is a nice idea.

Having read the reviews of the food, we stayed clear of any dish that could come out overcooked. One should note that the food is not the reason for going. That said, we ate very well on the house salad, crispy chicken livers, vegetable pot, and macaroni and cheese. The wines are of excellent quality. Now for the real reason to go: the atmosphere and music are top notch. Finally, the service was well above average and very friendly. Don't hesitate!

For starters the food was horrible. I had the Lamb Shank the portion was large but it was not well seasoned and delivered well below room temperature. My side dish was the cabbage with ham bits DISGUSTING! it was burnt and over cooked and too sweet only 2 fork tastings and then I pushed it to the side YUCK!. My friend ordered the fried chicken which looked like road kill and very dry her side dish was suppose to be mac & cheese NOT! it was more like baked ziti oh but that dish was hot though. If this was Minton's idea of soul food I give it a D minus. The only reason I gave this review 2 stars is because the ambience was nice and the music was awesome. Please improve the chefs southern cooking skills especially since the location has major competition of soul food restaurants in the area that also include live music FOR FREE! opposed to Minton's charging $15 to $25 cover charge that's simply RIDICULOUS. So here is my breakdown 
1. Food was nasty (my friend and I agreed on this)
2. $15-$25 cover charge turns away patrons 
3. Food temperature not up to par
4. The best part of the night was Alyson Williams and her band encore.
If you need a southern cook maybe my 84 year old mother can help you

I took one of my friends last night who was visiting from Singapore to Minton's last night. I just moved to Harlem and had heard it was a nice atmosphere. 

Pros:
* Music was world class and the sound system made the music very enjoyable
* Even with the music we were able to have a nice conversation within our small party
* Food was okay. Gumbo is probably really a jambalaya but tasty, snapper was good, deviled eggs and crab cakes appetizers were tasty, but the house salad was a little wilted. 

Cons:
* Service, service, service ...not very attentive or on top of things
* Service on drinks...I asked for a champagne with St Germaine and after coming back to the table 5 times asking about how to prepare it, to say that they only have one champagne and not the 3 on the menu, he finally comes back to say they don't have St Germaine. A friend ordered Riesling and then they refilled her glass with Pinot Gris which was the drink I had ordered previously. I ordered a Fitz for my second drink and it was horrible. 
* Service on food- we had someone join our party late and after 45 mins after placing the order we asked if her entree was ready which then came but it was now warm instead of hot. 
* watched a party of 4 in the lounge leave after they waited an extended amount of time for a server to come help them. 

After a 3+ hour ordeal they did comp the second drink but really wish the experience could have been better. I really want these establishments in Harlem to thrive and the neighborhood to be known for spectacular service.
Delicious food, delicious drinks, friendly and attentive service, good music. I am a fan. The shrimp and grits were really great, as was the salmon, gumbo, and yams. Definitely go to this place.

Had the most amazing experience at Minton restaurant. First of all I made reservations through a company called truly experiences for my boyfriend 25th birthday.. The experience included 5 course tasting menu( EVERYTHING AMAZING MACRONI IS SPECTECULAR) .. also the chef brings out one of the meals.  And the singer of the night sings happy birthday. The service was so perfect and just made us feel so special. Definitely recommend to all the jazz lovers and anyone lookijgnfor great southern food.

I visited this restaurant on August 1st with 5 other people (groomsmen). I'm not exactly sure where to begin. Overall, this place was nice. The decor was very nice and set the mood for the music. The band was entertaining...I believe they were the Biggish Band. The singer who went "Billie Holiday" on Saturday was amazing! Even the inside jokes between the band members, singers and random camera guy was entertaining. The food was good. Everything was flavorful and clean. The plates were small considering the price of the meals but overall it was nice. I had a Prima drink, delicious. Well made. The groom's drink was a bit strong smelling so he did not finish. If this was what the review hinged on, I would give Minton's a 4.5 or maybe a 5. But it didn't
The maitre d was the worst. We noticed the preferential treatment that was given to other customers immediately. The maitre d took the time to pull the chairs out for some of the other customers (males and females) and help them sit down. Not for us. Not only that, when calling for the maitre d, we noticed we couldn't get his attention even if we had a signal flare and 3 boxes of roman candles. So the 2 star demotion was because of this gentleman. 
The waiter made up for it. He helped us with pictures, he helped charge one of our party member's phone...and for that, he received a nice tip. I hope he doesn't get screwed out of it. He definitely deserved it. 

I probably would return to this place but it wouldn't be high on the list because I don't think I would want to deal with that maitre d again. 

OH! And for the trumpet player in the Biggish Band (middle guy next to the trombone player), get that guy a harmon mute and a cup mute. You have skills, but the sound doesn't work with the area. The harmon mute would give it more of a swanky sound for the blues. Even a cup mute would help a bit (cup with straight mute).

For many of us (not big into jazz, don't live near Harlem or the 2/3, A trains) a trip to this spot is for the experience, the history, and quite frankly to change things up and get away from your normal, neighborhoody or trendy spots. I'm giving it 4 stars because we had a great time...however. not sure I'd go more than 1-2 times a year due to one big drawback. But first...

The positives....
The band was great (The Willerm Delisfort Project) - and my guess is the acts are on a pretty solid level so that those of us that don't enjoy jazz regularly, will still have a great time. 
The ambiance was really enjoyable. Very laid back, slick, and polished (or seemingly so) and is very conducive to the atmosphere the music sets.

The okay....
The food. We had the prefix as nothing on the menu jumped out to us, except for one of the sides (peanut butter collared greens...eh). The apps (Chilled Corn Soup & Salmon Hushpuppies) along with one of the entree's (the Pan Roasted Salmon) were really enjoyable, very solid. However, the rest of the meal...the pork chop was like rubber, my knife was useless and the desserts just completely missed. The S'mores backed Alaska was close to tasteless and looked odd, while the meyer lemon tart was waaaaay to tart.

The eh....
Service was all over the place. The servers are really friendly and seem like they want to give you the best experience possible...but, as a whole it wasn't working. Our drinks came scattered (you'd think the bartender would complete an order in full), the soup was served without a spoon, and our sides came 3-4 minutes after the entrees were served.

The big negative, this place is really expensive. I'm fine with paying a cover for music, that's pretty par for course. But the cost for the food and drinks is beyond overpriced. I'd really like to come back here to hear more great music in that setting, but when the evening starts at $20 pp just to sit down, you need to give me top notch food if you're charging top notch prices.

Had an awesome time. The food was absolutely amazing. You must try the southern fried chicken with the potato salad, shrimp and crab gumbo a day baked alaskan. Upon walking in you are greeted by top notch service and an appealing and warm ambiance. I would like to thank our server, Shi, the manager, Kyle and the assistant manager, Stephanie for the impeccable attention to detail from start to finish. I highly recommend this establishment for anyone who is looking for a classy place to relax with friends or lovers!!!! I wish you guys much success and prosperity.

Such a great venue with amazing music. The ambience is beautiful inside - makes you feel like you've gone back in time. Went with a bunch of friends, however, you should know this isn't really the place for a lot of convo, since the live music is so good. We heard the Biggish Band and two singers. The ensemble was fantastic. What a treat. Only reason this got 4 stars from me was because the Pan Roasted Skuna Bay Salmon dish I ordered was alright. The pea purée in the dish was a bit too heavy for me. Salmon was flavored well on top (where the crispy yummy skin was), but the flavor didn't really permeate through as well as I would have liked. 

Other than the food (I'm also just a pretty picky eater), the place is great. It's nice to dress up and go out for a fancy evening, and Minton's is the place to do that.

I'll start by saying the food is amazing!!! I'd recommend the gumbo and the pork chops... However, when I visited the performance was good but not life changing. Also, the host that introduced the musicians was pretty tipsy and seemed a little disoriented. This by all means is a classy and historical spot, but with the negatives and the fact that a night out here for two could easily get you into spending over $300 I don't know if it's worth it.
:-/

I really want to give this place a five star... But I had to stop because the service I had received was pretty terrible. I think we slipped through a crack between waiter and hostess communication but we sat there literally for 15 minutes without water or anything and waited for our service. We eventually got several waiters to help us but the service was just horrible. I would normally give a service like this 1star but i have to say the music and ambience was just amazing!!!! I think it would be a perfect place to take out of town guests or for special occasions. I just hope you get a better service than us!

Fantastic place for date night or if you enjoy music with your meal. If its still available, definitely get the Groupon thats being offered for Mintons. The Groupon includes two appetizers, two entrees, a dessert, and two cocktails. The music was lovely, and the food is what im really going to focus on. Definitely have the crab cakes and mac and cheese. Both were cooked to perfection. But the shining star for me was the salmon. I am going to have dreams about that salmon for a while. Perfectly cooked rare, the crunchy skin, and the bean sauce and vegetables were blended so well.
A must try.

The perfect place to take someone you only want to talk to intermittently. The music fluctuates between being big and loud and being on the softer, more mellow side. The food and wine are great, though a bit heavy for my taste. I had the trout, which was a bit too rich, but the perfect creamy grits made up for it.

This was my first visit. The atmosphere was awesome, intimate. The music was excellent as well the night I visited. I ordered the shrimp and grits which was very tasty but short on shrimp. Next time I will try something else service could have been better but I had a wonderful evening with friends.
Very classy and absolutely everything I expected. Service was superb, drinks were great, and music was divine.

3.5 Stars

It's been a minute since I've been to New York and I had forgotten that their restaurant scene is on point (just like my favorite city....Chicago). There were six of us dining here for brunch. 3 of us got there right at opening so the restaurant was empty, but they still don't let you sit until your whole party is there. That was okay, except we couldn't even get a drink at the bar and the bar tender was looking quite flustered and confused. He couldn't find anything so we decided to wait to order drinks once we were seated.

There's a fee to eat at the restaurant cause you are paying for the jazz band. That Saturday it was Christopher McBride and he did an awesome job. Can't wait to hear him in chicago next week.

As for the food....mostly everything was 5 stars:
Mac and Cheese - by far my favorite. We shared 3 of these. The cheese was unique.

Collared greens - delicious and such a robust flavor

House cut fries - yummy

Bacon - okay. One order was good and the other one was too burnt 

Fried chicken and flap jacks - chicken was dry and not enough syrup on pancakes

S'mores dessert - ummm hello...delicious 

Strawberry Tart - okay. I'm not really a fan of warm strawberries.

Drinks were good, service was much to be desired (the wait for anything was a bit much), band was great, and food was pricey. Around $100 a person. Good place to try out at least once though.

Food was good. I had the Country Breakfast. Grits could use some work. The  service was def lacking. We were ready to drink and enjoy some jazz, but the drinks took forever. Overall experience was nice. Jazz was great.

Good music and food but if the hostess misrepresents information about the charges the management is not receptive and does not take responsibility for the error and that is why we will not be returning to this establishment.
Great jazz brunch on Saturdays and Sunday's. I had open face fried egg sandwich with salad on the side. We also had mimosas, okra, and sausages too. All in was $60. Great music and good food!

So we went to Minton's this afternoon, when we entered we were greeted by a friendly young lady who showed us our table. The first thing we noticed was that the manager had a very bossy attitude and walks around if she is your royal highness the Queen herself. This had in my opinion a very bad reflection on the customer service, she was talking in a certain manner that wasn't expected from a small cozy restaurant in Harlem. Nevertheless we decided to order and ordered some cocktails and country style breakfast. Unfortunately my smoky bloody marry wasn't as bloody (too light on tomato juice) however this was resolved pretty fast by our friendly waitress. After a short wait a waiter arrived at the table without mentioning even one single word, placed the plates and as both of us were rather surprised that our food was there not to mention the presentation of the plate (it looked like dog food to me) he finally could speak however as well with lots of attitude 'country style breakfast right?'  So our reaction was a simple 'uh yes' and that was it, no 'enjoy your meal' or anything in that genre. As we found this place through "open table" and we picked this spot as there was indicated 'live jazz' which was the case however just upon our arrival they stopped playing - the tricky thing was that the manager still charged us $10+tax per person as 'music charge' as I didn't agree with this they removed it however the fact that she (the manager) didn't bother to put it on while we didn't listen at anything else than a cd playing gave me a bad taste and decided to write this comment. Overall impression; the restaurant is a cute small place with lots of opportunities however the customer service and presentation of the food could be much better. The manager should be a role model and not sitting on her throne and treating this place as her kingdom as it truly takes the charming factor away from it. Would I recommend this place? No, unfortunately I won't as it wasn't a great experience after all.

Thursday, May 7th, 2015 was my mom's 82nd birthday.  We took her here to celebrate.  The beginning started out good.  We had appetizers and drinks.  The lead vocalist playing that night informed the crowd to support them by "making noise" as they played, and we did.  After the set, a woman (Paula) came to our table of 8 people and informed us to "lower our voices"...SAY WHAT!!  Mind you, there was a full house that night and other people were making noise as well.  I told Paula that the vocalist said to make noise, and she was surprised...like that was her first time ever hearing a table of 8 people make noise...REALLY?!  We are in a JAZZ spot where MUSIC is NOISE TO YOUR SOUL!  BB King (rest in peace), Dizzy Gillespie, Sara Vaughn, etc., would be very disappointed with Paula.  She left the table, and my niece was ready to bounce up out of there, but we all stayed because mom wanted to hear the jazz music. It took me a while to settle down, but after a couple of music sessions and drinks, the rest of the evening went okay.  The vocalist sang happy birthday to mom and she loved it.  I had the buttermilk fried chicken and did not like it.  It was tasteless and raw toward the bone when I bit into it.  The "silver dollar" sized cornbread was highly over-priced!  The collard green stems were also too sour!  All in all, I am sure that I spent more than any other patron in the house (over $800) that night!!  That being said, I will not be coming back here anytime soon...and, it's a shame because Matt was such a good waiter to our table that night.

Well...let's begin by saying I'm a humongous jazz fan and really really want this place to happen.  Minton's is a legendary jazz shrine - the home of bebop - and I was jumping up and down DYING to try it out and set foot on sacred ground.  And musically, the night went just fine - Johnny O'Neal was a pleasure to hear.  The room was fine - a bit underwhelming, but there are nice banquettes and upholstered chairs and the original mural on the wall behind the stage and it's Minton's and so no one's complaining, even if it isn't all I imagined it might be (the bathrooms, for one thing, were strictly utilitarian) - it must have been essentially a dive back in the day (a dive featuring Charlie Parker and Thelonious Monk and Dizzy Gillespie.)  And okay, the service is a bit rough - they're well-meaning and chatty, and warm, but too quick to take plates, that sort of thing.  But the real issue is the food.  The cocktails were okay - my hubby's was a bit watery, but mine was fine.  It was about the food. 

So let's get down to it.  My crab cake was fine - a crab cake.  Not complaining.  But his octopus arrived surrounded by a chilly cold salad with strawberries that were white - as in, not ripe.  It's May, so there are plenty of ripe strawberries available.  No reason to use unripe strawberries.  And the cold salad up against the roasted octopus just made everything seem cold.  It wasn't such a great start. 

Entrees were a bigger problem - I'm vegetarian, so I ordered the only dish I could order, the sole vegetarian entree, which was essentially a Japanese purple yam, baked, with some creme fraiche and a dab of caviar (okay, so I stretched on my vegetarianism and ordered the caviar.)  Without the caviar, it would have been super bland - as it was, it seemed more like a side dish (it even arrived in a little side plate, not even a real dinner plate.)  Not bad tasting, really, but Minton's is charging TOP DOLLAR for everything - as expensive as anything could cost in Harlem.  So it was a bit of a let-down.  Felt like $20+ for a potato and sour cream side dish. 

Meanwhile, my partner's fried chicken - the "signature dish" of the restaurant, was unforgivable.  The chicken was obviously frozen and undercooked. And it was surrounded by pickled vegetables - not bad, for home pickling, but that was it.  No mashed potatoes and gravy, no biscuit (we ordered two biscuits and paid about $7 for them - a separate appetizer order, amazingly) but this chicken was badly prepared and came surrounded, in fact drowning in, pickled string beans and black-eyed peas, etc.  He almost sent it back.  The lady at the next table - another vegetarian - did send back her expensive Japanese sweet potato.

The dessert was fine - strawberry and rhubarb pie - although it was both of our birthdays, and frankly, we expected the server to do a bit more than simply light a candle - they might had sent a slice of cake or a free drink or *something* more.  The wine list is actually rather good, although - like everything else, pricey. 

What can I say?  I want this place to succeed.  I'm a huge jazz fan, and this is the temple of jazz.  Please, people.  You can do better.  Don't be so greedy with the prices - or at very least, come through with the food for this money.  The chef seems to have some idea what he's doing, so smack him upside the head and get him to knock it off with being cute and just put out a decent plate of food.  Please.  This is Minton's.  And I want it to work.  The NYTimes gave this place as merciful a review as it possibly could.  But people around us were sending plates back to the kitchen and grumbling.  It's a problem.  We'd come back - but we need to see some indication that you're going to get your act together.  

The music is magical (although, yes, we're paying top dollar for that, too.)  Please pull it together with the food.  And polish the service.  And maybe stop being quite so greedy with the prices in general.  Mostly - just make it a decent meal.  This is Harlem - and you're serving Southern food.  Bad fried chicken is simply unforgivable.  And you're going to go down in flames when Harlem diners taste what you're putting out.  It's not rocket science.

Decent place to meet friends for drinks.

I went for midnight breakfast. So that's what THIS review is for.

You def need advance rsvp. 
Portions are very small...for what is suppose to be breakfast dish. And dishes were not "breakfast" like.

Prices were too high for portion/quality. $18 for a very small sandwich you can eat in 3-4 bites.  
My friend ordered this & sadly she was unfulfilled. Then had bad diarrhea at home. Thankfully I didn't ask for a bite..not that she could afford to share.

I had the duck hash. They must have forgot the duck...all I kept eating was potatoes. $18 for a pot of sauteed potatoes. Lucky for my hungry stomach, potatoes are filling...so that was the only benefit of that dish. Otherwise, I still wonder where if the 3 shreds of strings I saw were suppose to be the duck or were they potato skins?

I did get a side of biscuit. Nothing grand. 

I did not try any of the alcoholic drinks.

They had good DJ...crowd seems to be having fun.

I would not do the midnight breakfast again nor recommend it. I can come to have drinks or check out other events the venue offers.

I had the experience of dining at Minton's.  I really looked forward to having a pleasant evening. My husband and I were greeted very warmly the waiter was top notch.  

My dissapointed came when we were told that we had to get up from the table. We had just ordered a second drink , which I didn't finish,  little embarrased but we got up within 5 minutes.  The person we came to hear started singing at 7:50pm by 8:10pm we had to leave.   When I spoke with the young lady at the door I asked if there was a time limit.  She said "yes there is a two hour time limit and its on our web site."   First of all it was not indicated on my "Gilt Voucher" and I went to the Minton's website and didn't see it either.  Throughout my dining experiences when you pay for the music you get to at least hear the first set then you may have to leave.  That's understandable.    

My rating would have been much higher - Atmosphere, food was good but the way we had to leave was appalling .  This was a planned evening to eat and enjoy the Tribute to "Bille Holiday"  getting up 20 minutes was a blatant disrespect to the performer. 

I appreciated the fact that Manager contacted us which showed me that he was concerned.  However my evening was memorable in a negative way.  As customers we should have been advised that we had to leave the table but could at least sit at the bar and finished hearing the first set of music.  When there are restrictions and time frames the customers should be made aware of this prior to sitting down and enjoying a good evening.  Pleasant customers bring many returns!

Classic jazz spot In Harlem rich in history and soul. 


We came here to experience a lovely performance by Andy Bey. Its a very intimate environment; without a doubt a classy date spot with a mature crowd that genuinely loves jazz. There is an extra surcharge for a table by the stage, which I think is completely worth it if you're taking a girl out on a date and having a real dinner. Otherwise the seating by the bar is pretty far back by the entrance and while I'm sure the acoustics are great, I know I wouldn't have enjoyed my experience as much. 

Bear in mind that I wouldn't recommend this as a first date get-to-know-you spot and the reason is this: before the performance begins, talking is recommended to be at a minimum (hushed whispers...if at all). The layout of the place is that you and your date will sit by the wall- super cozy, which does make whispering easier. I remember we were really trying to hold in our laughter a couple of times. lol 

Portions are ginormous- I ordered the shrimp gumbo and barely made a dent! Service is excellent, and the servers were exceptionally courteous. 

side note: for the ladies- you'll see some people really dressed up! The lady sitting next to me the next table over was wearing what looked like a gown. No joke. I wore a simple dress, cardigan, heels and didn't feel out of place. Its a classy place so accessorize appropriately and you'll be fine :)

*This review is for the brunch only*

I have visited the sister restaurant right next door (The Cecil) on several occasions. While I know both locations have brunch on the weekends, I noticed Mintons had a jazz brunch; therefore I KNEW I would try this brunch first. 

When you walk into the location, you instantly feel like you are back in 1930's Harlem waiting for one of the great jazz legends to hit the set! There are pictures of jazz legends on the walls and the decor is extremely elegant. I also enjoyed the intimacy of the restaurant and the ability to sit anywhere and have a full view of the band.  That brings me to the band...

These four men were incredible! It was clear they have been playing for years together. We were advised that one of the songs was composed by one of the members.  Each member is extremely talented and definitely added to the memorable experience. Well worth the $10 music charge.

The food is quite tasty. The red velvet pancake and fried chicken was excellent. We enjoyed the brunch cocktails as well.  The service was attentive and knowledgeable of the menu, a great factor when visiting a restaurant for the first time. All in all, we were extremely satisfied and will be returning!

Was there 4/11/15 for a special tribute to Billie Holliday with a party of 5. We paid the $25 cover for the bar and took our seats. The problem is that the dining section is between the bar and the stage. The diners would talk OVER the music and even at some points start shouting to each other to be heard when the music got louder. Our server also informed us during the set that we would have to leave soon and that there was a two hour limit for our seats. We already knew from the website we were paying for one set so to interrupt during the first set to inform us we'd have to give up the seats was rude and a bit insulting to our intelligence. It is also a basic move to make if you want to make your patrons feel uncomfortable or unwelcomed. It was my first time there, on a suggestion by a musician in the Saturday house band at Minton's, to check it out. I invited my friends and their out of town parents from LA on their last night in the city. It was really disappointing. The music was top notch if you could focus on it above the loud din of the diners. The drinks were expensive $14-16 (on average) considering the experience.The manager on duty was unresponsive to two requests from us to speak to him, first on the loudness of the adjacent dining table (their waiter actually told me the shouting wasn't normal), and about the server. I was also hoping to find a jazz place that was more of a local spot but sadly I don't think many from the neighborhood were actually there (as patrons). A huge disappointment.

I love Minton's. It's one of those special places where you feel like you have stepped back in time... getting to experience something that is unique to nyc. the music is out of this world. can't wait to go back.

A gem in Harlem, this place is perfect for an intimate dinner or a special night out. If I could give it six stars, I would. The service was stupendous beginning to end from the warm welcome to the personal goodbye. I took my girlfriend here for her birthday and we will definitely be back. 
The cocktails are named after classic jazz musicians and singers, as is each individual menu giving the restaurant a special touch and the diners a quick lesson in jazz history. The classy décor, live jazz band and separation from the outside world really makes you feel as if you have escaped to a place and a time forgotten.  
Get the water lily buttermilk biscuits! You'll want two orders, trust me. 
For the dessert, I would recommend the Fried Apple Pie and the S'mores Dessert. They are both like nothing you have ever tasted before.

Food was excellent! I had the pork chop and my friend had the duck. We were both very pleased. Service was good, our waitress was attentive and gave us good recommendations when we were being indecisive. Our desserts were just as impressive as our meals! We had the pineapple upside down cake and the s'mores which had ice cream in the middle. I was really happy when I realized this because clearly I did not read the full description. The music was very nice as well. It was relaxing and nice to hear live music while we ate. We will definitely be back!!

1st time experience was bitter sweet...Lets start with the fact that we were not informed of the $10 fee for live music at time of reservation...Found that out at the door.... Ambiance was great, food was great, music was great... Disappointed that there was no more coconut for the "Pineapple-Coconut Cocktail", pineapple alone did the job...Baffled at why "Chicken and Waffles" was ordered, but "Chicken and a Pancake" came to the table... We later learned that the waffle maker had broken... Nonetheless the dish was delicious! 
After some time, the manager did came over to iron things out.
Oh... And after paying the bill the waitress came back to the table to question her service because she noticed she got less than 18% tip... Really?! 
My fault for mis-calculating... But really?
Overall... Food and Vibe was great... Great for an intimate date... Based on my 1st time, service and communication needs improvement.

The food was amazing
The jazz band was amazing
The ambience was amazing
The waiters were amazing

Will definitely go again.

What can I say "Southern Hospitality @ its best!" From the general manager greeting you at the entrance, to the very charming bartender Michael and staffer Matthew (Mat). By the way did I mention how handsome the male staffers are? Now onto the live jazz band and the delicious food. Kudos to the pianist, she was just amazing. The food and the drinks incredible. I couldn't get enough of the crab cake. This was my first time at Minton's but believe me it won't be my last!

Minton's captures everything it was suppose to capture, a time traveling experience to a old restaurant and jazz house known for such wonders as Dizzy Gillespie. The food however is an attractions alone by itself and the fact that Alexander Small the restaurateur  happened to be there, made the attention to detail and the overall execution stand out even more to us.

The interior is beautiful and the staff were all very friendly. 
For the food, I would say 5/5 chicken liver pate; 3/5 short ribs; 4/5 fried Apple pie. 
Couple of things to watch for: $50 cancellation fee if you need to cancel less than 24 hours before your reservation. $50 charge per person for "music fee". Glad I got to check it out for Restaurant Week, but not a place I would pony up for otherwise.

Same experience as Jen D. Have been a loyal fan of both The Cecil and Minton's since they opened. Two weeks ago made a reservation for two for restaurant week.  When we called Minton's today to find out if there was a later option for our reservation tonight we were then told there would be a $50 cover charge. We asked why they didn't call or let us know initially ... no explanation. 
I live one block away. I want both of these places to keep succeeding. Passing this along in the hopes that the fabulous places they created don't get a bit sullied by some behavior somewhere along the line with their representation.

Found out about  Minton's during the NYC Restaurant Week. Came here for dinner on 2/22/2015. If you're not careful you would walk/drive pass it (pay attention ). Its an intimate setting. As you enter you are drawn into the Jazz era. 
My one gripe was the first course. I had the "oxtail rillette", it was off.  For supper I had the "Buttermilk Fried Chicken" delicious doesn't justify how great it was. It was perfectly fried and paired with green beans, and pomegranates (had my taste buds all over the place). My date had the "Duck Cassoulet". I had a few bites it was also delicious but mine was way better. Dinner was paired with Sangiovese (go for the bottle, it lasts all night). For desert we had a peanut butter and chocolate cake. 
The staff was on point. Patrick is the man he was so attentive, and had the answers to whatever questions we had.  The music was out of this world. Definitely making another reservation and I've already recommended Minton's to a few friends.

didn't get to order food... A friend and I were looking at nyc.go restaurant week menus and wanted to try Minton's. I arrived and ordered a drink at the bar, two other parties arrived and were told about the $25 per person cover due to the band; I was not.  I heard the hostess mention this to the 2nd party and questioned it.  I had made my reservation on Opentable, never looked at the Minton's site and was not aware of the cover.  We left and found a lovely restaurant a few blocks away. I don't object to a cover charge and I am sure the band was good, but that's not what we went for and it was not what we expected.

The Jazz was good. However the hostess and food were not. The hostess was very dismissive, when we came the restaurant was almost empty, and reservations aren't accepted for brunch, but she still found it difficult to seat us. We returned later having confirmed that there was space over the phone, again couldn't reserve. When we arrived she wanted us to wait in the lobby even though there were tables,  she said because the waitress needed to catch up. Why she thought that meant we should stand rather than be seated at a table that was already laid and prepared escapes me. 

Then one of us ordered the open salmon sandwich with over easy eggs. We made it very clear that meant runny yolks. However they came very very overdone, not as ordered. If you are paying for the jazz separately the food and service don't have as much of an excuse to be bad, in my opinion. Perhaps next time I will just go to their bar for a drink and the music. The food is overrated and badly executed, small portions and expensive.

I ended up at Minton's because The Cecil had a private event going on and I wasn't invited (bummer). It was a Thursday, Minton's had a live jazz band playing that night (there's a mandatory $25 band fee); I went with the flow... The service was excellent, in spite of the fact that our server was training someone, that didn't negatively impact service, it only enhanced our experience because the new girl aimed to please. We made the mistake of sitting two tables away from the band, if I could do it over, I would have requested to be seater further away. The music was way too loud, not complimentary to dinner conversation. After screaming for the first few minuets, I gave up and just sat quietly... Tip: If you looking to catch up with a friend over dinner, don't go here when they have a live band. If you must go, try sitting closer to the exit.  Overall, the wine selection was great, we had a Malbec (blanking in the vintage) and the food was amazing, I had the gumbo.

My first two courses were incredible.... after starting with their paté, (which was accompanied by a simple but perfectly enhancing jam), I had the buttermilk fried chicken - it was the best fried chicken I have ever had. On the side, their brussel sprouts were extraordinarily flavorful, as was their interpretation of black-eyed beans. 

What makes the food so awesome here is the way that the chef manages to synthesize ingredients which are all local to the American continent. My biggest complaint about the cuisine served in some of the USA's best restaurants, is the paucity of flavor of its underlying ingredients - ingredients which are often not remotely indigenous here and which often just taste bland . Mintons takes the best of dishes from the South, whose foundational ingredients are really American too. The result: BEST MEAL IN MANHATTAN IN 2015 SO FAR!!
Wow, what a fantastic night of jazz. Classy restaurant and amazing musicians. Highly recommend anyone to come up here to see great jazz musicians. JC Hopkins and all of his guests were unbelievable.

This is exactly the kind of classy jazz place I didn't find in NOLA. We went on the Gilt deal and had a great time. Make sure you wear a jacket. You can go (classy) fancy here and not look out of place (I should have gone fancier). They have a coat check. The food is good. The music is great. 

Request a table nearer the bar/entrance side, as the live music, which is great, is loud and constant. We were sat right in front of the band, which made conversation more difficult. From the mid/back, you could have the best of both worlds. On a Saturday night, the set was 1 hour long, followed by a 25 minute break. There were short rests between songs.

The food is good, though not memorable. It is also spread out over several hours, which I thought, enhanced the experience. We shared a several plates of starters. The wagyu beef was the best. Then I had a ribeye steak. I asked for medium rare and it came rare. Should have sent it back, but didn't. .  

Service was very friendly, but didn't get every 100% right. 

Thoroughly recommend.

My wife and I spent New Years Eve at Minton's. Best New Years Eve since I was two. Reallyl great. Food special and service could not be better. The ambiance and perfomers made it an evening to be remembered. WOW.

Came here with a deal.  The deal allowed us to get the prix fixe, which was great (although I am not too fond of the entree [scallops], I still thought it was very good).  Food was good, but I would not go back for just the food - it's the jazz that will.

The music there is fantastic.  We were close, so it was a bit loud, but that was ok due to the fact that it was so good.  I love it here.  I will go back, deal or no deal.

This review is for their Sunday Jazz brunch. Let me set the scene for you...beautiful jazz music, amazing food, and delicious drinks. This four-hour (yes we stayed for four hours) experience was just what I needed that Sunday (after church of course). 

Minton's is very similar to its cousin next door, the Cecil (see my review for the Cecil as well). Minton's is a little more intimate than its cousin and that was the perfect setting for a lovely date-jazz-brunch. My boyfriend and I stumbled upon Minton's after church and what a gem we found! 

The one-star deduction is because the waiter seemed to devote more time to one particular table than the other tables and it was rather rude. Thankfully the lovely manager George was there to save the day! He really went above and beyond to make sure we were comfortable and enjoying our brunch. I can't remember the name of the jazz band but they were really really good! I know they rotate performers pretty frequently but I'm sure all of the entertainment provides a wonderful experience.

The food was great! Minton's (like the Cecil) provides an African-Asian fusion cusiine. I know on first glance that sounds like a LOT is going on and trust me I thought the same when I first saw the menu BUT whatever magician they have in the kitchen, they need to keep cause the meal was fantastic. I am still dreaming about that meal

I had the brisket over scrambled egg, fried rice and hoisin sauce. It was amazing! They put all of my favorites in one dish and it was incredible! The only complaint I had was that the rice was a little spicy for my taste, which was kind of weird, because...spicy fried rice...what? Still, loved the dish and would order it again. Maybe I can ask for less spice next time.

Way too expensive for what you get. Sleepy band, 14$ cocktail and small portion of the food. Great concept but done by people who aren't in touch. They also got rid of the original Mintons sign, a real piece of jazz history, Morons...

I rarely go uptown in Harlem but received  a Gilt voucher for Minton's. 
And I am very happy I had a chance to dine and enjoy the music.
It is a beautiful, classy place with very well dressed staff and patrons alike.
The host was very gracious, the bartender attentive, and the waiter patient AND very knowledgable. The cocktails were excellent, food was good (pricey if we were going to pay full price), and the music was just perfect. 
I was very impressed and and I will definitely be returning to Minton's with other friends and family soon.

A fun classy place to listen to music in the neighborhood.  Yes it might be a little overpriced, but welcome to NYC!  If you don't feel like spending too big, then sit at the bar have a nice cocktail and order some biscuits to fill up on while you listen to great music.

BEST JAZZ CLUB in the CITY! 

Bought a Gilt City Deal for my Father in Law's birthday and it was great.....

First of all, Open Table was acting up and my reservation never got to the restaurant BUT the hostess says "it's fine I will honor your reservation and seat you asap." She did not disappoint.  

Second, this place has a Dress Code...no jeans, no t-shirts, etc.  So great to walk through a dining room and see everyone dressed nicely! 

Third, the food.....oh em gee.  Great.  What can I say.  I had the Arugula Salad to start (yes, it's lame but I was eating super fatty for the main course...read on and you will see, lol).  The rest of the table had the mac n' cheese (it was Gouda! lol Corny)....and the fried Oysters.  Main course...there was the Rib Eye, the Snapper, the FRIED CHICKEN (that was me! lol) and the Duck!  Everything was prepared perfectly and sooooo good.  Desert was an Apple Pie and the Smores.  The Smores put me in a coma....it was SOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO good! 

Fourth, the entertainment....excellent!!! The staff was perfect.  The decor was great.  

We will be returning.  My father in law was thoroughly impressed.  So happy! Thank you Minton's!

My husband and I experienced Minton's Jazz Sunday Brunch. We had a wonderful time. The live band was great! The ambiance is very classy. The food was very good and the service was exceptional! It was my husbands birthday and the band was gracious enough to play a jazzy rendition of Happy birthday. We will definitely be back!

Let me first say that I am basing my rating on the full experience and what it cost.  My husband and I had a great Gilt City deal for the evening that included a shared first course, second course, 2 mains, a dessert, 2 cocktails, and music for $103.  THAT would have been 5 stars, absolutely!

The ambiance was really nice, our server was so polite, knowledgable, and paced the meal perfectly.  The music was INCREDIBLE.  10 Piece band and singers.  Fantastic.

However, the food was a real letdown.  Again, at the price we paid for the deal, good stuff, but the check would have cost $240 (our server included that in the billfold so that we would tip on what the meal was worth, no problem).  I had a $40 scallop dish that had 3 scallops and no more than a tablespoon of puree and 3 cauliflower florets.  My husband had the porkchop that was oversmoked.  The apps were fine.  We had the cheese plate for dessert, and at $18 retail, we were underwhelmed.

Minton's should take a hard look at their pricing and portioning.  We would love to return if things were a better value, but the food honestly didn't warrant that type of price point.  It was just ok...

Never have I felt so underdressed and classless. This place brings it! Beautiful music, well-dressed staff and patrons, and great selection of booze. They even provide a blazer if you dont have one on. 

To those who rated it low, I'd love to see what places you actually gave five stars to. Of course, we all have our own styles. I tend to rate places in comparison to other stuff in its respective category.

NO!
That's all I really want to write, but I know I need to say more.
Okay, so my male bff kept raving about this spot, I checked out the menu and was like O okay, we can go.  We get there, and it's really nice - cute, quaint, blah blah blah. Before we get seated, the hostess says there's a music charge. I am like cool b/c the the OLD SKOOL cool cats were playing - I did like the fact that the band was all races and they were jamming, but ah hem... wait for it.

So we walk to our seats and I am tyring to figure out why ALL  the seats directly across from the bar are taking - you don't have to pay the music fee, but you can hear the music - this place is NOT big.

Okay, so we sit, get the menus and I, as normal, ask a LOT of questions. Heck... I need to know what I am consuming.

So on to the food, I had a 59.00 plate of rice - okay, the rice dish (CHARLESTON RICE PILAU) was $25 , the music charge (per PERSON) was $20.00 and then there was tax and tip.  We, the others, had the SHERRY SHE CRAB SOUP - we immediately had to season it,  the LOW COUNTRY CHARCUTERIE  - who my male bff kept correcting the waiter pronouncing it wrong - he's SUPER EXTRA - I wanted to slap him,  the WILD ARUGULA SALAD, and the SEARED DAY BOAT SCALLOPS.  The total for the three of us came to 260 give or take $5.00 and we only had two drinks among the three of us. They, my folks and the waiter, kept trying to get me to get a salad, but I am NOT paying more than 10.00 for a salad with no protein. I can get a container of 50/50 mix at BJs for 4.49 (this is a main staple) - dude (Minton's is a dudish name) bye. Read it.. the food was just MEH and that's what I go to a restaurant for - the food. I am definitely willing to pay for GOOD food, but NOT for meh food. 

All in all, I will NOT go again and I am questioning my male bff's ability to pick stuff, his reasoning skills and our friendship ;)

Ambiance. Music. Service

Minton's is a TRIP ! A Voyage I should say, to a older, better, sexier Harlem. In an epoca where Gentlemen wore blazers to establishments and Ladies evening gowns. 

My boyfriend took me there for a "last minute" date nigh a day that I was wearing jeans, rain boots and military jacket. He had no Blazer either. ;-0 
(Thank you) modernity, there's no DressCode for Women and they provide Men with oversized blazers. 

This hidden GEM is a full experience from the entrance to the exit. The ambiance is Amazing, the Decor is perfectly Jazzy and refined, the staff is cool and sexy, the crowd is mixed from young European tourists to 60 years old locals... and young BK crowd with rain boots on LOL ! The Music is awesome and ever changing every night of the week from Tuesday to Sunday. 

The food is good. But that's about it. Nothing was stricking or worth to be that overpriced. We ordered red wine from Italy, Fried Green Tomatoes on a crab bed (tasteless), Crispy Shrimps and Oysters (fresh shrimps OK taste), Fried Shrimps and Spicy Cheesy Grits (likey but here again taste is very "White" like I like to call it) and Fried Chicken and greens. The Fried Chicken was AMAZING ! The batter very tasty and crispy and the meat super tender and juicy. Really a MUST ! The deserts are all (I tasted all) OK but not worth it really. 

I love Southern Cuisine in general and this one is no exception but I was a bit disapointed since the food doesn't reflect the overall quality of this place. I suggest going there for cool vintage cocktails or wine at the bar or for snacking on a late night. 

* They charge $20/pp for the music. $10/pp if at the back of the room. The prices are really high. Count $15 for apetizers , glass of wine or cocktail and $25 for entrees. 

Experience : 7/10
