@Bonjourclem

XOXO
Clem

I loved this place! I actually live close to Minton's and have never heard of it, was so happy to have found it. I have to give the credit to Gilt, they had a deal for them and I immediately snatched it up, it was definitely worth the price and then some.

This place is very nice, dressy, old school (men require jackets) and I felt a little Gilt-y (no pun intended :)  ) using the voucher, but the waiter was really nice and took it discreetly when we sat down, didn't make a fuss about it at all. He was very nice and  gave great suggestions, even told us what would be an extra charge for certain dishes, but let me tell you it's totally worth it. My date got the Lobster and Shrimp Grits for dinner, we sat down at 8:30, and by the time we got the dinner I heard him telling the table next to us that they ran out of that dish (really a shame for them!!). It was so very yummy.

For apps we ordered: Biscuits and the Mac and Cheese - Both were delicious
Second app: Fried Green Tomato - Another great dish
My dinner was the Scallops and I LOVED it.
Dessert was the Choc carmel cake thing - so very rich.

And the drinks were very very strong!

If you are looking for a jazz getaway in a place with a lot of history, and love getting dressed up and feel like you are back in time, go here! Loved it. Will be back.

Minton's is beautiful! The ambiance, the service, the decor, the live band- I would give this place 5 stars based on these things. BUT the food was not up to par for what we were paying. We had the pork chop and lobster which were sadly dry and lacked flavor. When you pay $40 an entree and your total bill not including tip is $240, there is a certain expectation. That expectation was not met. Also, if management is reading this, I think that you should notify people when they make their reservation of the $20 cover that will be added to the bill for the live music. I made my rez through Open Table and the confirmation informed us of the dress code and men needing to wear jackets/blazers but no info about the cover charge.

I don't want to knock Minton's too much bc I do love that someone is trying something so fancy and new in Harlem. Like I said, everything but the food was beautiful.

Visited during Restaurant Week. It is truly a posh "supper club". However, Mathew, our waiter, was the best part of the evening.  The food was pricey, and mediocre. By mistake I ordered "flat water". We had been offered a choice of tap, sparkling, or flat. It was $8.50 a bottle. A bit precious. We were told that there would be an additional charge for bread. We skipped it. Long waits for the food to be delivered. Plus the music although nice way way too loud. No way to converse with your dinner partners. I truly hope that Minton's will get their act together.

Minton's is a true Harlem gem.

We came here on a recommendation from a friend who lives locally who was waxing lyrical about the club as a true institution.

We love Jazz and also any excuse to get dressed up so it was a perfect spot for me to take the better half for a special occasion.

We booked a late seating (10.30pm) on a Friday night. I cannot recommend doing this enough. It's probably a little easier to get a table at this time than earlier in the evening but it really gives you the best experience as you get to keep your table through to when the club closes at sometime around 3am I think (my memory was a little hazy by that point).

The food was great, well made, simple southern comfort food, but jazzed up.  Some great cocktails on offer and even a selection of craft beers.

But the reason to come here is the vibe. The service is exceptional, the club owner was there when we were and will shoot the breeze with you through the evening with  good conversation. And as it gets later, the musicians mix it up and sit and drink with you, the stage becomes open to local musicians to just get up with the band and jam and nobody is on the table they started on but instead just spending time with new people.

I can only go on the one night we were there but those were the things that made it exceptional. Thank you to all involved.

Enjoyed jazz and dinner here. Mac and cheese served bubbling hot and creamy. Crispy trout with okra succotash was flavorful and nice. Drinks are strong. Ambiance is nice. Come to hear the music and not chat through dinner. Service was nice. Chef de cuisine was walking around and meeting diners which was a pleasant surprise.

We came for the superb jazz, and we will be back for the sublime food! A wonderful choice for a special night in Harlem. I especially recommend the gulf shrimp for the first course and scallops for the third.

The decor was lively but elegant, with a colorful, restored 1940's mural backing the stage -- the lady in red is said to be Lady Day -- and nicely mounted photos of the greats, including Parker, Gillespie, and Monk, who played here in the '40's, set off by a sleek layout and subdued lighting.  

My dish, delicately fried soft-shell crabs on a bed of spicy greens and citrus, was as good as those crustaceans could be. The service was friendly and efficient. (I had to withhold one star here because the prosecco they served was flat and nearly tasteless. However, I did not bring that to the staff's attention.) 

Some Yelpers complained about the white bread quality of the music. I can't comment on those complaints. But the night that I was there, a Tuesday, the featured group lived up to the quality and inventiveness of Minton's fabled past. From now until the end of August, the club will be presenting a Tuesday-night, Latin-infused series. If its upcoming acts are even nearly as good as the one from this week, they will be well worth your attention.

This was an exceptional dining experience! The ambiance was everything you'd hope a jazz club and restaurant to be. The decor of rich furnishings and subtle lighting added to the elegance. The food was excellent, I'd call it nouveau southern, extensive wine cellar, talented and attentive wait waitstaff left no stone unturned. The music tops the evening with old school jazz greats, what a lovely evening ,they can have my money anytime!

They can take my money whenever they want.  The service is high end above plenty of other places in the city as far as food goes. This was officially my first jazz experience in New York and I have to say I will be coming back quite frequently. 

The experience that you will have here will be perfect in terms of keeping it authentic when it comes to jazz. The jazz players I believe are the house band and they play very well and are from one of the oldest living generation of jazz players they definitely added a beautiful sound to the whole place their live performing skills were so pleasing to the ear and with the food I did not want to leave.

When it comes to conversation with the staff, they are very knowledgeable and the best part about the drinks I had was that they use Grotissimo Brandy cherries. 

I work in the food and beverage industry and I have to say I am very impressed. 

I am beginning to recommend this site to guests and customers that are looking for a musical experience while dining. 

One of the things you will notice on the way in is it's hidden location in Harlem. The neighborhood where it is located is very low-key but up-and-coming and if you know your history you will know how historically significant the area is for jazz and the Harlem Renaissance it is beautiful and elegant and very intrepid.


Go to Minton's.

5 stars for ambience and music.  Service was very attentive--lots of staff to meet your every need.  Chef makes visits to the dining room to answer questions regarding menu.  Great history and this support of this Harlem revival made for an enjoyable Saturday evening in New York. Not just a couples or family place--after all--it's the music!

Minton's was quite an exquisite experience. From the entrance at the door to the seating, the warmth of the colors and the portraits of the Jazz greats/era, welcomed us to a world of days gone by. The staff was very attentive and the food was a delight. We thoroughly enjoyed the live band as they played some fantastic jazz numbers. We will be happy to return there soon and we're inviting our friends along.

Great atmosphere and service.  Service was exceptional.  Food was good but not great.  Fried chicken was outstanding, some of the best I have ever had.  The pork chop was mediocre with a heavy gravy.  The crab soup was not mild without any real strong flavor.  Would go back and try other items and certainly order the fried chicken again.

The bonus of this place include the ambiance, we had a 6:30 reservation when we got there they had just opened  so my date and I sat at the bar. Every staff member was helpful and polite including our bartender. They did not rush us to our seats at all they simply said "no rush, whenever your ready just let us know" They even let us pick out a table and reserve it. Came right as the jazz band started playing.

Food:
Starters were crab suit and foie gras. Crab suit was tasty but it didn't quite do it for me but the foie gras was heaven on a plate.

Mains I had the venison pink and my date had the steak. Both cooked excellently and the Brussels sprouts were one of my favorite parts to the plate.

Dessert I had the white chocolate and my date had something else i don't remember right now but both were excellent.

The only complaint I have is the waitress who was opening a champagne bottle for the table next us and dropped it as she opened it and my date and I got sprayed from the knee down. The manager was polite in apologizing but alas words cant dry the champagne off me.

5 stars for the ambience, I would like to give the same for the service but I was ignored by some bust boys a few times and the waitress didn't come too often so there for lll give them 4 stars for the effort.
The food wasn't amazing, I was even served a cold steak that was quickly wormed up in a Microwave I assume (when they brought it back the plate was hot) we ordered a few things on the menu and nothing really blew me out of my mind.
The reason to go back is definitely for the music, ambiance and great cocktails.

I came with a large group of my friends to Minton's last Friday, and we had a great time. The live Jazz music really set the tone and was the highlight of the night. I had their mac and cheese which was very filling and cheesy (which is a food thing in my mind). Also, I had the pecan tartlet which was great if you don't like excessively sweet things like me for dessert. The only downside was that because such a large group of us came our group had to be awkwardly split into two groups at different tables. However, overall it was a nice time, and I'd recommend anyone who likes jazz music to check it out.

This restaurant  had  great reviews and I have wanted to try it since it opened. Based on this dinner with three other people, I won't be back. The cauliflower app was encased in a soft, greasy dough; ditto the paneer. The crisp eggplant was excellent. The various types of nan were routine. A Brussels sprouts dish was oily and tasteless. My goat in the goat curry was very tough. A rice pudding was flavorless, we left it. Over all, the food was under spiced  and wickedly expensive. Service was fine. The restaurant is attractive with pretentious hosts. The thumping music made me hoarse and gave me a headache. All four of us said that we won't be back. 
I think that the Michelin man needs to pay this place another visit.

The atmosphere and dining room of this restaurant are aesthetically pleasing. Impeccable service. We were seated at the table right next to the stage - we were given the option to move if we felt that the music was too loud, but I prefer to be up close when there is live music so we opted to keep our table - it was loud though so it will hinder convo if you're close. I thought the band was cute - it was made up of older gentleman and one older woman on the piano - I believe that some of them played at the original Minton's but I could have made that up... They were actually really good, but the song selection was a little dry, slightly boring, but I enjoyed it nonetheless. I ordered a cocktail based on the suggestion of the waiter, good choice b/c the drinks were strong (just the way I like them). Had the smoked gouda and gruyere mac & cheese and the grilled gulf shrimp as appetizers and both were REALLY good. Ordered the sweet potato ricotta dumplings as my entree which was fairly bland and tasteless. I was really disappointed and wish I had ordered something else. My dining-mate ordered the grilled rib-eye which was fantastic! I'm not a huge meat eater, but I probably will comeback to have the steak. For dessert we shared the pineapple upside down cake which was also very good. Dinner and 3-4 rounds of drinks for two people, I believe put the bill around $300. I definitely will go back to try a few other menu items, but I can't see myself frequenting this restaurant too often until the jazz up the entertainment a bit.

This place is legit.

Great place to take a dinner date or even an old friend to catch up with.

This dimly lit diamond in the rough is definitely a place to check out if you like good souther style food accompanied with great jazz.

I know that Harlem can be a travel for some people, but I highly recommend giving this place a shot.

The service is very friendly as well.

came here for my sister's birthday. surprised her. the mood was great, as was the food, and the music. BUT we were seated and had an extremely long wait for a waitress or SOMEBODY to come and just take a drink order. right off the back, our waitress rubbed us entirely the wrong way. she was rude and not welcoming. she didn't really come back and when she did, it felt forced. i was upset by this, as i was surprising my sister. who the heck wants bad service for their birthday. we were so ready to get out of there even though the food was great and everybody else seemed helpful. we asked for the check. that took a while. our party split the check. she came back 20 minutes after and said she accidentally charged us wrong amounts. then the manager had to fix it, which took some time as well. but ANYWAY i'm writing this review, because i just checked my account, i was overcharged by 100$. nahhhh.

Jazz and sophisticated southern cooking, what else can a man ask for. Oh hot waitresses too. We came here after Christmas day for a little music, The menu was a bit constrained, not the usual full menu it was a Sunday night.

1.Fried Gulf Shrimp and Oysters  Charred Okra, Sweet Pepper Remoulade 

2.Braised Pork Belly  Johnny Hoe cake, Fried Organic Egg, Country Tasso Ham Bearnaise 

3.Deviled Egg Toast  Smoked Trout, Country Ham, Pickled Shallots
4.Buttermilk Fried Chicken  Red Skin Potato Salad, Three Bean Salad 
5.Grilled rib eye (4)
6..Crispy Fish & Grits  Red Eye Gravy, Pimento Cheese Grits, Braised Cabbage
7Sweet Potato Ricotta Dumplings  Chanterelle Mushrooms, Coconut Collard Greens

And plenty of drinks, the music was good and the food very good.
.

Came here with girlfriend on a Saturday night before starting our 5-borough adventure (well almost all) She reminded me of how pathetic we would look sitting in an actual table just the two of us so we sat at the communal table in the front and looked like we were the girls checking in the guests since its upon entering the resto! We quickly overlooked all of that once the amazing drinks came! I had the Blood & Fire and she the Sahara Nights...it was so good I just wanted to cradle it and not drink it! Then came the Gumbo! Wow! we got the large portion (by mistake) and it was more than enough for 4ppl! Since we didn't realize there were 2 sizes our pretty server made the adjustment and off we went into the cold winter night.. bellyful and full-of-feels thanks to the cocktails! 

A bit pricey but definitely worth it...spent $73 for 2 cocktails and the small gumbo & tip!

Awesome atmosphere, perfect for a special night out.  Paid about 200 for 2 with cocktails.  Food was great (had the rib-eye and salmon) and the entertainment was awesome.  

I didn't think the menu which included fried chicken and fist and grits, matched the atmosphere but maybe that's just me.

The folks at Cecil certainly did a good job revamping Minton's (which was a classic Harlem jazz club): they maintained the original decor and layout of the place (including the distinctive mural behind the band), but reorganized dining tables so that they are now to the 2 sides of the room with space to dance in the middle. Service and vibe is excellent, and I would certainly come here just to stay at the bar and catch some good jazz played by adorable old-timers. Dinner is definitely on the expensive side ($300 for 2, but with $150 going just in wine) but is not bad: the low country mixed appetizer is a must try, and then I was a fan of the pork chop - really moist and smoky flavorful thanks to the collard greens. The venison was somewhat underwhelming due to lack of seasoning, but overall the experience was good.

Had an OK dining experience at Minton's.

The place is aesthetically pleasing, and can certainly get one "in the mood" if that's what you're looking for.

Unfortunately, I ended up paying $250 for dinner for two, and 2 drinks. And also, as a jazz musician - the houseband plays some really white-washed, boring standards.

Felt like a tourist attraction, as opposed to the REAL minton's vibe.

Overall, a cool spot but highly overrated for the price point, quality of the food, and quality of the music.
Great atmosphere, great music, comfy place. Food pretty good, but tries a bit too hard.

Overall we had a fine experience but sadly we cannot make this a go-to because it is so expensive. $90 a head is steep anywhere but in Harlem I can't see how this price point is going to be sustainable unless it becomes a destination. The service was mediocre which is sadly the case in most Harlem restaurants (except Vinteria where it is excellent). The jazz was a little disappointing - I was hoping for some jam sessions but it felt a little more like background music. The "house musicians" are on salary I hear so I get that this is a job for them but it could be a little livelier. Maybe of they had special guest musicians and change the prefix format we could be inspired to go back.

Nice to have real live jazz music in Harlem!  I think the food was good but a little over priced.  Yes, you are paying for live music and the band was excellent!  A little annoying they called three times to confirm reservation and kept mentioning men need a jacket, got it the first time.  Definitely worth the trip if you like live jazz.  Service was excellent, attentive and friendly.  Will be back just to sit at bar and have a few drinks.

I'm so SO bummed out. We had high hopes - after all, it's our neighborhood and we LOVE the Cecil, Minton's sister restaurant. 
Hoo boy. They're clearly still working out the "newbie" kinks. The service was really, really bad. From not having a clue about their wine list to forgetting drinks and dessert, then charging us for a dessert we didn't have...it was embarrassing and we couldn't wait to get out of there. I realize this is not ENTIRELY the restaurant's fault - it's the server, who'll likely last another day before screwing up the wrong person's order...
Then the fire alarm (strobe lights and all) went off for FIFTEEN MINUTES! Holy moly - it was so bad. Nobody came to our table to apologize or even let us know what was going on. All the while, the music played on. I get it - this is NYC and things happen - can't always help it, but the least management could have done is stop by each table (it's a small place) with a courteous apology and sheepish smile!
Finally, the food. It was good. Not amazing, nothing I can't get next door at the Cecil for 1/2 the price, but if I go back I'll sit at the bar. This place needs serious work before a reconsideration!
Huge disappointment!

We went there last Friday night and had an amazing experience from start to end. The band, ambience, food, and service were all fantastic.
I had the foie gras and the ribeye steak, and my steak, on the contrary of one of the other reviewers, was thick and very tasty. One of my friends ordered the mac and cheese, which was di-vi-ne! My boyfriend had the venison and was really happy with it. 
We had cocktails, and they were also very good too.
For dessert we shared the banana cream pie and the vanilla pound cake. Both of very nice and delicate but we specially liked the banana cream pie.
The jazz players were so talented that the almost 3 hours that we spent there went by super fast.
Overall it was such a special night and we will definitely be coming back and bringing new people over. 
Harlem needs more places like this, and I really hope that this place will continue to be a success.

This place overall is good for a special night. $300 for 2 with drinks. The ambiance and service were excellent. The jazz music during dinner is very good and 2 hours goes by quickly if you are watching the band.

 I'm rooting for this place to make it, so some constructive criticism would be around the food and size of the cocktail. My ribeye steak was very thin and flavorless. It was not steakhouse quality for $46, worth maybe $29 at most. I realize you are paying for the music too, but I feel the steak could be much better. The Mac and cheese was fantastic, as was the down home or low down appetizer of 5-6 items. I almost ordered a second of the down home appetizer. The bread biscuit was excellent too.

The red wine selection and prices are pretty bad and says "expense account" all over the wine menu. I was looking for a $60-$90 bottle of Cabernet or red. Two choices for red by the glass, and the $16 Gamay was low quality. My Manhattan was well made, but filled up an ounce short of where a $15 drink should be.  

Overall great experience and we will be back. I am glad an option like this is in the neighborhood. We enjoyed dressing up and soaking in the history.

If you come looking for a nostalgic New York then come here. The Mac and cheese is creamy, the pork chop is smokey like bacon, the greens are official, the Brussell sprouts rustic, the grits gritty :), the crab cake all crab, ribeye hits a bullseye!!!!! 
Service is good, alittle forced but I appreciate the effort. Practice makes perfect. Now the band.... There are no words. Old school players doing their thing, well!!!!!!! One of my best nights ever. $300 for 2 well spent! ($90 per person minimum-awkward)

Minton's is as good as it gets but gentleman beware, you must wear a jacket for entry into this establishment.  An older way of thinking no doubt but setting the tone for a unique experience.
Jazz plays 40 minutes on, 20 minutes off and usually the classics are played that any generation of jazz lovers would know.  We sat at the bar (due to the $90 table minimum per person) and ordered the 2 drink minimum.  I had the lady day and duke, which were made with love by our mixologist.  
I loved this place and would highly recommend it for the sect that wants to have a conversation with company (and actually hear them) but also are looking for a certain ambience that is hard to find in todays social ecosystem.  It's traditional, classic and modern all at the same time.

questions.question: Are the tables reserved or on first come basis?
questions.answer: Better to make reservations cause they only have very limited walk-ins I believe. They also require you to purchase tickets for some of their shows. Better to purchase a ticket and call them for the reservation.

questions.question: How is the ability to park nearby?
questions.answer: It really depends on the night. Weekdays will probably be easier than weekends for street parking. Not sure about paid garages in that area.
